items.title: How the biggest renewable energy project in US history finally got built
items.summary_raw: When the sun goes down, the wind picks up in central New Mexico, whipping through arid canyons with a ghostly howl that for centuries, locals have likened to the wails of the folkloric ghost La Llorona. A few hours east of Albuquerque, this June, those gusts began powering the largest wind farm this continent has ever seen, twirling over 900 colossal steel turbines. Each is as tall as the Statue of Liberty, scattered across a patch of desert roughly the size of Chicago. They plug into a 550-mile transmission line stitched across the Southwest and are now powering over 1 million homes — as far away as California. The SunZia Wind and Transmission project is a rare 21st-century triumph of American infrastructure, an engineering marvel that generates more electricity than the Hoover Dam. When the turbines came online this spring, they immediately broke records for wind-generated power in California’s energy supply, where solar power may rule the day, but the winds of New Mexico increasingly fuel the night. After years of stagnant power growth, the U.S. is absolutely starving for more electricity, with demand projected to rise by 25 percent by the end of this decade , and a staggering 78 percent by 2050. Enormous as this challenge might seem, it may ultimately be the catalyst the country needs to dramatically dial up its renewable energy infrastructure, so that the years to come are powered not by gas or coal, but by clean energy sources like the sun and the wind. By next summer…

items.title: The EPA is quietly killing its web archive
items.summary_raw: In a little-noticed webpage update, the Environmental Protection Agency has announced a plan to decommission its online web archive at the end of the year, a move that would wipe tens of thousands of publicly available environmental resources from the web. The discreet banner notice comes in stark contrast to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin’s recent public takedowns of the agency’s power plant pollution standards and federal methane regulatory system . “The EPA’s online archive makes information about a wide variety of environmental issues and past policies available to the public, dating back at least 20 years,” said Gretchen Gehrke, co-founder of the Environmental Data and Governance Initiative, or EDGI. “This information is irreplaceable, and if the archive is decommissioned, that information will be lost forever.” For decades, the web archive has been an unparalleled resource for researchers, legislators, policymakers, and the public writ large. It houses everything from fact sheets and environmental reports to agency policy changes and regulatory actions, making it a tool for “ democratic oversight ,” according to Gehrke, who for 10 years has been tracking changes to vulnerable federal environmental data. Screenshot of the EPA’s online archive webpage Rachel Santarsiero This isn’t the first time the environmental agency has tried to shutter the online web archive. In late January 2022 , the Biden administration’s EPA announced plans to discontinue the online repository…

items.title: Trump cut funding for farmers — then unlocked billions for them before Election Day
items.summary_raw: The last two years have been a rough going for farmers and ranchers in the U.S. Rollbacks to several Department of Agriculture programs have cut available funding and left producers in the dark. Last year, farm groups sued the federal agency after it deleted multiple webpages that mentioned climate change, including some with critical information for planning around extreme weather. (Early this year, the ag department agreed to restore the webpages in a settlement.) Just this month, the USDA cut solar from a popular renewable energy grant program and dealt another setback to farmers who wish to lower their utility bills and pad their incomes by installing solar panels on their land. Meanwhile, cattle ranchers in the U.S. have been frustrated by high beef prices. The average price of ground beef has been steadily climbing since the COVID-19 pandemic, reaching new records in the last two years. Persistent droughts contributing to historically low herd sizes have also added to ranchers’ plight. And President Donald Trump’s various moves to supposedly help lower the price of beef — such as importing more beef from abroad — haven’t helped. Ranchers even say these trade deals undercut their business model . So heading into the midterm elections, many agricultural producers, once a critical part of Trump’s base, have been clear that they’re aggravated by and disagree with the president. items.summary_raw: Understanding green tourism choice behavior is crucial for fostering and sustaining tourists’ participation in sustainable travel. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) (Ajzen, 1991), this study aims to examine the structural determinants of individual green choice behaviors among tourists. A cross-sectional survey was conducted, yielding data from 403 domestic tourists visiting the Mekong Delta, Vietnam. Data analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) indicate that green tourism demand and environmental protection attitudes positively influence participation intention, which subsequently drives recalled green choice behavior. Furthermore, the findings reveal a positive, albeit weak, direct effect of climate change awareness on environmental protection attitudes.. The paper concludes by offering grounded managerial implications for sustainable tourism development and outlining clear directions for future research.

items.title: Socio-spatial patterns of energy citizenship components in contemporary Hungary
items.summary_raw: Energy citizenship has recently emerged as a key concept in the social sciences related to energy transition, yet its definition, components, and societal manifestations remain underexplored. This paper contributes to this discussion by analysing the socio-spatial patterns of energy citizenship components in Hungary, based on a representative national survey ( N = 1000) conducted in early 2023. Based on literature, four constitutive components were operationalised: participation, pro-sustainability energy-use practices, prosumerism and pro-sustainability attitudes. Using hierarchical cluster analysis, we identified four distinct societal groups: everyday reduction practitioners, highly aware citizens, disengaged consumers, and transition pioneers, each featuring specific socio-spatial profiles. Our findings reveal that energy citizens characterised by the high level of all constitutive components are not identifiable as a distinct social group in the Hungarian context, instead, the components of energy citizenship appear in fragmented combinations across the population. This challenges ideal-typical views of energy citizenship as a coherent social condition and highlights contextual factors, including structural constraints that shape citizens' agency in becoming energy citizens, including housing type, available infrastructure, resources, the policy context and political culture. Our findings, beyond their scientific contribution, offer guidance for differentiated policy…

items.title: Frames and Counter-Frames of Meaning in Climate Change: Between Public Percepti
items.summary_raw: Objectives: This article critically examines how frames and counter-frames organise political and media communication about climate change, with particular attention to frame production, media and platform circulation, reception by polarised audiences, and contributions from environmental journalism and environmental education. Methodology: The study uses a structured critical narrative review of peer-reviewed scholarship, combining foundational works with recent studies published mainly between 2023 and 2025. Searches used combinations of climate change, framing, environmental communication, environmental journalism, climate education, polarization, misinformation, emotions, and solutions journalism, together with DOI metadata and publisher pages. Results: The literature indicates that climate framing cannot be reduced to a Lakoffian account or to a simple opposition between information and emotion. Journalistic practices, political identities, platform logics, environmental education, responsibility attribution, and efficacy beliefs all shape interpretation and engagement. Conclusions: Rigorous climate communication should combine scientific evidence, psychological and geographic proximity, frame plurality, transparency about interests, and credible responses, while avoiding both paralysing catastrophism and overly moralising or reductive narratives.

items.title: A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security research

Floods, droughts, and irregular monsoons, as manifestations of climate change, adversely affect crops, farmers' livelihoods, and food security. A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security (CCFS) research can indicate progress and emerging research directions on adaptation and risk-management practices, supporting farmers, policymakers, and investors in decision-making. Methodology Bibliometric analysis was conducted on articles and book chapters published between 2002 and 2024 in Scopus-indexed journals. The keywords “climate change” AND “food security” were used to retrieve documents, with the search constrained to economics, econometrics, finance, and social sciences. Bibliometric indicators, author keywords, research themes, and international research collaboration were examined. After manual screening, 2,366 documents were selected for analysis from 14,188 retrieved records. VOSviewer and the Biblioshiny package were used for science mapping and performance analysis. Results Publications and cumulative citations on climate change and food security increased over the study period, reflecting growing research attention to climate-related risks to food systems. Where intention goes, responsibility flows: Grounding AI accountability in the machine learning paradigm
items.summary_raw: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and postdeployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: Trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor’s responsibility by their intent’s specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology’s pace…

items.title: Reply to Zhou and Tsao: Synergy rarely underlies the benefits of combination cancer therapy
Mechanism of catalytic regulation by an allosteric hot spot in dihydrofolate reductase
items.summary_raw: Allostery is central to catalysis and regulation, yet how distal perturbations control enzyme activity remains unresolved. Here we elucidate how a distal allosteric hot spot regulates catalysis in dihydrofolate reductase, a benchmark enzyme exhibiting latent allostery. We combine enhanced conformational sampling, reactive free-energy calculations of the chemical step, and perturbation-induced nonequilibrium molecular dynamics with evolutionary analysis and experimental kinetics to obtain a comprehensive molecular description of conformational landscapes, catalytic activity, and allosteric communication. We show that a mutational perturbation at the hot spot redistributes the populations of two globally similar conformations with a subtle but critical structural difference that makes one catalytically competent and the other not. Nonequilibrium relaxation simulations further reveal that the transition between these two states in the mutant proceeds through a stepwise sequence of local structural rearrangements rather than a concerted global motion. Guided by this mechanism, we rationally engineer a compensatory second-site mutation that partially restores activity. These results provide a unified thermodynamic and kinetic view of allostery and establish a general, mechanistically guided framework for engineering allosteric regulation in enzymes.

items.title: In-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling
items.summary_raw: Constitutive modeling is fundamental to computational solid mechanics, yet most existing approaches remain material-specific and require retraining or recalibration when materials change. Here we introduce In-Context Modeling (ICM), a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling that infers constitutive behavior from physical context rather than material-specific optimization. Using hyperelasticity as a testbed, we demonstrate that ICM can be trained once on equilibrium deformation fields spanning diverse materials, geometries, and boundary conditions, enforcing physical equilibrium without stress labels. After training, the same model can be directly deployed on previously unseen hyperelastic materials without retraining. At inference, ICM treats a small set of nonuniform strain fields as physical context to generate constitutive response in a single forward pass. Numerical benchmarks and experimental validation demonstrate accurate stress prediction across out-of-distribution materials and boundary-value problems, together with substantial reductions in deployment cost compared with per-material learning approaches. These results establish in-context learning as a retraining-free paradigm for constitutive modeling, particularly valuable for heterogeneous biological tissues such as the brain, and suggest a pathway toward foundation models for computational mechanics.

items.title: HAR1 receptor kinase links nodule autoregulation with repression of auxin signaling and lateral root development
items.summary_raw: Nitrogen-fixing root nodules develop as lateral organs on legume roots and their formation is restricted by autoregulation of nodulation (AON), a systemic mechanism with unclear evolutionary origins. We identify Lotus japonicus NUCLEAR FACTOR Y subunit A4 ( NF-YA4 ) gene as a central target of the leucine-rich repeat receptor kinase HAR1, which controls both AON and root system architecture. Under nonsymbiotic conditions, HAR1 suppresses expression of NF-YA4 and its close paralog NF-YA1 , at least in part through a miR169-dependent mechanism, mirroring the Arabidopsis CLAVATA1/2-miR169- NF-YA module. Loss of HAR1 leads to NF-YA4 overexpression, broad transcriptional reprogramming, and induction of LATERAL ORGAN BOUNDARIES DOMAIN , STYLISH , and YUCCA auxin biosynthesis genes, enhancing auxin signaling and lateral root development. Grafting experiments show that HAR1 constrains NF-YA4 -mediated branching both locally in roots and systemically from shoots. Because NF-YA4 functions partly redundantly with NF-YA1 to mediate nodule emergence, our results suggest a model in which duplication and neofunctionalization of an ancestral NF-YA-dependent pathway controlling lateral root development facilitated its recruitment to the nodulation program. They also raise the possibility that AON could have evolved, at least in part, through the co-option of a LRR-RK/miR169/ NF-YA regulatory module that limited lateral root development.

items.title: Deep mutational scanning of the GPCR rhodopsin reveals pleiotropic mutational effects and their roles in modulating receptor signaling
items.summary_raw: Biophysical pleiotropy, the phenomenon in which a mutation affects multiple protein properties, underlies many genetic diseases and shapes protein evolution, yet remains poorly understood, limiting synthetic biology and therapeutic development. Although extensively studied in soluble proteins, little is known about how pleiotropic effects shaped the evolution of receptor protein functions. Here, we developed a cell-based assay designed to assess pleiotropic effects in G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs), the largest receptor class in eukaryotes. Because our assay allows for multiple GPCR molecular phenotypes (basal activity, ligand-dependent signaling, and cellular receptor abundance) to be simultaneously assessed, we applied it to study rhodopsin, a visual GPCR that evolved for high phototransduction capabilities by maximizing light-driven responses while minimizing noise. To investigate this, we integrated our assay with deep mutational scanning to test the impacts of ~2,000 single-residue substitutions in rhodopsin across all three molecular phenotypes (~6,000 measurements). By analyzing these data in the context of rhodopsin’s protein structures, we found complex pleiotropic effects that act asymmetrically to impose joint constraints, restricting mutational tolerance in rhodopsin’s retinal binding pocket and G protein interaction interface. A dose–response analysis of rhodopsin signaling revealed that these pleiotropic constraints arise from the dual functions of its…

items.title: Origami state machine with time-varying magnetic fields
items.summary_raw: Achieving reliable, remote control over multiple stable states in modular systems remains a challenge due to the coupling between modules and history-dependent transitions. Here, we present magnetic origami state machines that enable deterministic navigation from any unknown initial state to any target state under magnetic actuation. By assuming mutually distinct energy barriers in modular Kresling origami assemblies, we realize fully accessible transition graphs with scalable state spaces. Guided by the graph associated to the state machine, a rotating magnetic field induces a universal reset that autonomously drives the system to a known equilibrium state from arbitrary states without sensing or feedback, while pulsed magnetic inputs further enable programmable transitions to any target state via prescribed actuation sequences. A reduced-order Lagrangian mechanics model predicts snap-through dynamics across reset, stepwise programming (between graph nodes), and shortcuts (by adapting pulse magnitude and orientation) where inertia triggers simultaneous multicell transitions with a single pulse. These results establish a general framework for programmable magneto-mechanical state machines with autonomous state reset and full state-space control.

items.title: Multiscale Brownian dynamics simulations reveal effects of macromolecular crowding on protein–ligand association
items.summary_raw: Macromolecular crowding is known to influence the diffusive, binding, kinetic, and equilibrium properties of proteins in a range of environments such as occur inside biological cells or in highly concentrated solutions of protein therapeutics. However a quantitative understanding of the effects of macromolecular crowding on the rates of protein-small molecule binding is lacking. Here, we present an adaptive model to simulate the association of two solutes in a macromolecularly crowded environment using Brownian dynamics and to compute the corresponding bimolecular association rate constant. The adaptive model represents interactions with atomistic detail for short-range crowder–noncrowder interactions, while using a coarse-grained approach for long-range crowder–noncrowder interactions and all crowder–crowder interactions. This multiscale approach is integrated in the Simulation of Diffusional Association (SDA) software for Brownian dynamics simulation of biomolecular diffusion. We applied this model to compute the rates of association for two contrasting protein-small molecule inhibitor complexes in environments varying in macromolecular crowder type and density, and we used Markov State modeling of the encounter trajectories to analyze the binding pathways. The results reveal competing effects: While the presence of the crowders can hinder ligand binding by reducing the translational diffusion rates of the solutes and obstructing the protein binding sites, crowders can…

items.title: Structural basis of glycoprotein recognition by the human folding sensor UDP-glucose:glycoprotein glucosyltransferase
items.summary_raw: UDP-glucose:glycoprotein glucosyltransferase 1 (UGGT1) plays a central role in quality control of glycoprotein folding within the early secretory pathway, yet the molecular basis of UGGT1 substrate recognition remains poorly understood. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of human full-length multidomain UGGT1. Monomeric UGGT1 structures reveal two conformational states corresponding to “open” and “closed” architectures. Three-dimensional variability and molecular dynamics simulations suggest the existence of intermediate conformations, leading to a model in which a continuum of structural transitions underlies UGGT1 function. Notably, in the open state, the EM-maps reveal at the top of the U-shaped protein a density that bridges the sensory TRXL2 and the glucosyltransferase catalytic domains, consistent with substrate association. This observation supports a mode of binding that places the substrate near the catalytic domain. A dimeric form of UGGT1 was observed in which the glycoprotein substrate binding sites are occluded, suggesting that dimerization may regulate UGGT1 activity. To better understand the spatial relationship between the site of misfolding and that of UGGT-mediated N-glycan reglucosylation, we identified N-glycosylation sites on endogenous glycoprotein substrates by glycoproteomics. items.title: Strange, catastrophic landslides are kicking off across the far north
items.summary_raw: Nearly a decade ago, a helicopter pilot flying in Canada’s Northwest Territories noticed something peculiar: a landslide so immense, it had blocked a river and created a lake . But that damming power wasn’t what made this slide so strange. What he saw wasn’t just new to the landscape, it was new to science, what researchers have dubbed a “permafrost detachment slide.” In a recent paper , a team of scientists describes two of these events in the region, one stretching for three-quarters of a mile and the other for 2 miles. Combined, they’d moved 30 million cubic yards of earth. Whereas other kinds of slides send a torrent of rainwater and mud and rock down a hillside, permafrost detachments happen when frozen soils degrade and the land fails catastrophically. Weirder still, the two slides started three decades ago during a wildfire, which slowly transformed the permafrost until the land collapsed in a matter of hours or days along the Johnson River in 2017 and Redstone River in 2018. When the researchers visited the slides, they found them embedded with chunks of frozen material up to 650 feet long. “It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” said geoscientist Joseph Young, lead author of the paper, who conducted the research while at the University of Alberta. “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.” Permafrost is a major planetary wild card . Simply put, it’s ground that remains…

items.title: What’s fueling Indonesia’s worst wildfire season in a decade?
items.summary_raw: A government bus outfitted with oxygen tanks. Fire fighters collapsing to the ground in relief at the first sign of rain. Dozens of orangutans rescued. And hundreds of Indonesian students marching through the haze, some wearing gas masks, others carrying signs that read, “If we burn, you burn with us.” These are recent scenes from Indonesia’s worst wildfire season in a decade. More than 4.6 million acres have burned across the country since August, blanketing its large island regions, like Kalimantan and Sumatra, in a thick smoke that has spread to neighboring countries. Millions are breathing in this toxic haze, and the government’s data shows that more than 300,000 Indonesians have sought treatment for acute respiratory problems. On some days, the air quality conditions are more than 13 times worse than the threshold considered unhealthy. And like in many tropical countries, buildings in Indonesia are often built to maximize air flow, rather than filter it or keep it out. “This is a public health catastrophe,” said Robert Field, a fire researcher at Columbia University. Although there are other pressing consequences of the fires, such as carbon emissions and the harm to wildlife and forest habitats, “it’s hard to think much past the air quality issues,” he said. The fires are the latest environmental crisis inundating Indonesia. The country is not only one of the world’s most populated, but also one of its most disaster-prone . The resilience contract: Comparing climate resilience planning and community realities in Dominica
items.summary_raw: Climate resilience plans are proliferating globally, yet whether the priorities they formalise align with what communities themselves are identifying as essential for resilience remains unclear. Dominica has pledged to become the world's first climate-resilient nation by 2030; its Climate Resilience and Recovery Plan (CRRP) was produced following Category 5 Hurricane Maria in 2017, which resulted in losses of approximately 226% of GDP ( The Government of the Commonwealth of Dominica, 2017 ). We compare the resilience framings embedded in the CRRP with those emerging from 101 interviews carried out across Dominica in 2024. We identify strong community networks and social capital as strengths while economic insecurity, limited access to finance, and inconsistent institutional enforcement emerge as persistent weaknesses. Six components interviewees identified as central to resilience – faith, flexibility, family, activism, disaster aid, and evacuation – did not emerge as distinct components in our coding of the CRRP's 56 national initiatives. Drawing on state legibility and adaptation social contract theory, we introduce the resilience contract: the perceived arrangement through which actors understand what resilience requires, who is responsible for producing it, and how well those responsibilities are perceived to be fulfilled in practice. We describe these unrepresented components as being policy-imperceptible – their significance in lived accounts is not translated into a…

Policy Portfolios for Green Technology Innovation: An Evolutionary Game Analysis of Heterogeneous Firms
items.summary_raw: Abstract Enterprise-led green technology innovation (GTI) is pivotal for achieving China’s “dual carbon” goals. This study develops a heterogeneous-agent evolutionary game model to evaluate how a portfolio of market-based policies which contains environmental taxes, carbon emission trading, and subsidies influences the innovation strategies of large and medium-sized enterprises (LMEs) versus small and micro enterprises (SMEs). By incorporating “innovation success probability” as a key parameter, our model analyzes the individual and synergistic effects of these instruments. Our findings are threefold. First, policy effectiveness is highly contingent on firm scale; SMEs require significantly stronger policy support than LMEs to adopt GTI as an evolutionarily stable strategy. Second, a combined policy portfolio is markedly superior to any single instrument due to both synergistic and substitution effects, which allow for flexible regulatory design. Third, external factors such as the “technological dividends” stemming from intelligent supervision, the “institutional dividends” from optimized tax structures, and the “dynamic efficiency dividend” arising from firms’ “learning effects” can amplify policy impact, thereby creating a pathway to Pareto-improving outcomes. Our heterogeneous-agent evolutionary game framework captures firms' differentiated responses to climate policy instruments, revealing when market-based policies succeed or fail in inducing genuine technological…

items.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
items.summary_raw: Abstract Electric power systems are evolving into cyber–physical infrastructures shaped by power electronics and digital control. As inverter-based generation alters system dynamics and digitalization heightens vulnerability to errors and attacks, cyber–physical coupling can also introduce subtle system-level effects. Here we show that grid-frequency time series worldwide exhibit a persistent 1-min oscillatory pattern whose origin has remained unexplained. We show that clock-synchronized control software in digitally controlled energy devices, particularly uninterruptible power supplies and battery energy storage systems, generates periodic power-demand peaks that propagate across voltage levels and can give rise to the observed pattern. The pattern amplitude has increased substantially in several grids over recent years, contributing to wear and tear in hydropower systems and motivating stricter frequency-control requirements. The rapid expansion of battery storage, data centres and the Internet-of-Things may further amplify such cyber–physical power oscillations, highlighting the need for improved control design.

items.title: “That’s why the crops are here” - Perceptions on extreme weather events and grape growing in Brazil’s semi-arid region
items.summary_raw: Abstract Extreme weather threatens global grape production, which depends on an annual harvest cycle. Unlike most viticultural regions, grape cultivation in the São Francisco River Valley (SFRV), northeastern Brazil, requires irrigation, a condition that enables two annual harvests and has attracted investment in recent decades. Although the region presents predictable dry seasons, an extended drought from 2011 to 2019 severely affected agriculture and livelihoods in the Brazilian semi‑arid zone. Amid ongoing climate change, we hypothesize that growers within Public Irrigation Projects (PIPs) perceive themselves as relatively water secure, potentially reducing their sensitivity to drought severity. Using Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) and in-depth interviews, we documented stakeholders’ recollections of extreme years and their perceived impacts on viticulture and daily life, contextualized by river flow dynamics and observed precipitation. Growers identified intense rainfall during expected wet periods as more harmful to production than extreme dryness. Multilevel governance of the São Francisco River—particularly releases from the Sobradinho Reservoir and irrigation districts—has buffered local water supply from regional declines, shifting the main production risk toward intensified rainfall and overlapping hazards that require coordinated, multi-level adaptation.

items.title: ENERGY SECURITY AND THE CASPIAN STATUS: A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF PUBLIC STRATEGIC RISK PERCEPTIONS
items.summary_raw: This study combines legal analysis with empirical data on public risk perception to examine the impact of the Caspian Sea legal regime on Azerbaijan’s energy security. While the 2018 Aktau Convention is a milestone, unresolved delimitation issues and environmental concerns continue to pose strategic risks. Using a survey of 433 participants and statistical analysis (Factor Analysis, Regression), the study reveals that Geopolitical and Cyber risks are the main drivers of overall risk perception. Furthermore, regression results show that increased awareness of environmental and security risks is significantly associated with public support for the transition to renewable energy sources. The results suggest that ensuring Azerbaijan’s long-term energy security requires not only resolving legal disputes in the Caspian, but also accelerating green energy diversification to reduce perceived environmental and geopolitical threats.

items.title: Climate Change and Citrus Production: Multi-Stress Physiology, Rootstock Selection and Adaptive Orchard Management
items.source_name: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology
items.summary_raw: Citrus is an evergreen subtropical perennial whose long fruit-development cycle exposes orchards to several climatic hazards within a single season. Warming, more frequent heat extremes, altered rainfall, declining irrigation-water quality and episodic freezes now coincide in many producing regions, yet the physiological, genetic and agronomic literature on these hazards has developed largely in separate compartments. This critical narrative review examines how the evidence on combined abiotic stress, rootstock-mediated tolerance and orchard-level adaptation fits together, and how far laboratory and pot findings can support decisions in commercial orchards. Peer-reviewed literature published from January 2000 onwards was identified through international and regional scholarly sources, supplemented by citation tracking, and appraised qualitatively for design, stress realism, scale and transferability. Four conclusions are well supported. First, combined heat and drought produces physiological responses that cannot be predicted from either stress alone, with leaf cooling through transpiration, photoprotection and antioxidant capacity distinguishing tolerant from sensitive genotypes. Second, rootstock rankings are stress-specific and frequently reverse between seedling experiments, grafted pot trials and field orchards, so that no rootstock is broadly tolerant. Third, regulated deficit irrigation applied at less sensitive fruit-growth phases can save water with modest or no…

items.title: An extra beat every minute
Fear and alterity in The Kerala Story (2023): affective politics and the construction of Muslims in contemporary Indian cinema
items.summary_raw: The article explores how the film The Kerala Story (2023) functions as a site of mediated political discourse, and harnesses affect, spectacle, and a fear-based storyline strategically framed as fact to normalise majoritarian sentiment. It interrogates the representation of Muslims in a tale that depicts young women caught in a web of deceit, religious conversion, and radicalisation. It treats the film as a vehicle that channels a broader discursive framework of sectarian hostility. The analysis draws on the director’s interviews, narrative framing, and selected film scenes to identify three interlinked dimensions of fear and demonstrates how the film mobilises emotive appeals that have the potential to deepen communal divisions and harden religious identities along Hindu-Muslim lines. Rather than limiting the analysis to the question of whether the film’s Muslim stereotyping is inherently Islamophobic, the article examines how such portrayals align with, reinforce, and amplify a prevailing political ideology and majoritarian dogma within its narrative universe. Its artistic choices are structured to invite audiences to categorise Muslims as a civilisational threat within and beyond the fictional world.

items.title: Assessment of Community Acceptance of Hydrogen and Alternative Liquid Fuels (H2&ALF) in Nigeria: Bridging Environmental Goals and Public Perception
items.source_name: International Journal of innovative inventions in Social Science and Humanities
items.summary_raw: The growing need for environmentally sustainable energy across the globe has raised the level of interest for Hydrogen and Alternative Liquid Fuels (H2&ALF) as feasible sources of energy apart from the traditional fossil fuels. Although the use of such energy sources is economically and environmentally viable, the successful implementation of the process hinges on the level of acceptance and perception of the public. The empirical evidence on the same is still scanty especially in developing countries like Nigeria. This study evaluated the community acceptance of Hydrogen and Alternative Liquid Fuels (H2&ALF) in Nigeria with particular focus on the linkage between environment and public perception. Descriptive survey research design was used. Data was obtained through the use of a self-structured questionnaire which was distributed to respondents using the Taro Yamane sampling method. Descriptive analysis using frequency, percentage, mean and standard deviation were applied in analyzing the data. The results indicated that the respondents have shown good perception of hydrogen fuel and alternative liquid fuels because of the environmental benefits associated with them and their potentials in promoting sustainable energy development. Some challenges that can impact the process include public awareness, safety, policy implementation and infrastructure preparedness. It is concluded that environmental education, stakeholder involvement, transparent government policy formulation…

items.title: Future-ready livestock systems: climate resilience, animal welfare and sustainable adaptation
items.summary_raw: Climate change is increasingly challenging the sustainability, productivity, and welfare of livestock systems worldwide. Rising temperatures, prolonged droughts, water scarcity, changing precipitation patterns, and emerging disease risks directly affect animal health, welfare, feed availability, reproductive performance, and farm profitability. These pressures are particularly pronounced in climate-sensitive regions such as the Mediterranean, where livestock production is closely linked to limited natural resources and highly variable environmental conditions. Strengthening the adaptive capacity of livestock systems therefore requires an integrated approach that simultaneously addresses animal welfare, environmental sustainability, technological innovation, and farm resilience. This paper examines key pathways for developing climate-resilient livestock systems by integrating animal-based, environmental, technological, and management strategies. Particular attention is given to climate-adapted breeds and genetic resources, heat-stress mitigation, improved animal health and welfare management, adaptive grazing, sustainable pasture and forage management, integrated crop–livestock systems, and efficient use of water and other natural resources. The potential of precision livestock farming, digital monitoring, sensor-based technologies, early-warning systems, and data-driven decision-support tools to anticipate climate-related risks and improve adaptive management is also…

items.title: “Every professional is a climate professional”: a framework for climate responsibility in practice
items.summary_raw: Professionals are an important class of actors often overlooked in efforts to address climate change. Across fields such as health, law, education, the built environment, and media, they combine specialised knowledge, institutional authority, and public credibility, giving them a distinctive capacity to translate sustainability science into practice, reshape organisational systems, and coordinate climate action within their domains. This paper conceptualises professionals as a distinct class of climate actors and develops a generalisable framework for how their expertise, ethical values, and institutional authority can generate systemic change. We treat the professional role as a socially constructed position, formed first in higher education and then through accreditation and institutional norms that can unintentionally reinforce unsustainable practices. Universities and the bodies that accredit their programmes are therefore central sites for forming climate-ready professionals. Building on this, we set out a framework for enabling climate-aligned practice, organised around three interrelated stages: crisis translation, which frames climate change as integral to a profession's mission; ethical activation, which grounds climate responsibility in professional values; and institutional pathways, which shape how climate action is enabled or constrained by professional bodies, training regimes, and organisational systems. These stages operate across multiple levels, from…

items.title: Acceleration of the global methane growth rate over two decades: comparison with shared socioeconomic pathways and implications for future modeling
items.summary_raw: The Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) are a set of harmonized greenhouse gas emission and concentration trajectories, representative of scenarios from the literature. The SSPs show a particularly large range of methane (CH 4 ) trajectories early in the first half of the century, with vastly different implications for near-future climate warming. Using global concentration estimates from NOAA’s Global Monitoring Laboratory and observation-constrained global atmospheric methane estimates from NASA’s Goddard Earth Observing System (GEOS) model, we show that atmospheric methane has been accelerating from 2001 through 2025 with oscillating variability, and that both the trend and variability are driven by microbial emissions. Based on the current trend, we expect average CH 4 concentrations to align most closely with those of the SSPs associated with severe warming by midcentury. Continued atmospheric monitoring and further investigation of the microbial processes that may be causing this increase, including both agriculture and wetland climate feedbacks, are necessary to produce realistic predictions and mitigation scenarios.

items.title: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
items.summary_raw: Abstract Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. To this end, we conduct 100,000-year-long simulations for different CO 2 conditions using the community Earth system model coupled to the bihemispheric Penn State University ice sheet–ice shelf model. Whereas global warming exceeding 2 °C above pre-industrial conditions and related subsurface ocean warming lead to the millennial-scale disintegration of the West Antarctic ice sheet, the East Antarctic ice sheet shows a much greater resilience, even at 10 °C or more of warming. The simulations reveal that a moister and cloudier atmosphere over Antarctica, with southward-shifted westerlies, increases snow accumulation and reduces shortwave radiation. For Greenland, a 6 °C threshold above pre-industrial levels is identified. Capturing the balance of ocean- and atmosphere-driven ablation and accumulation processes in coupled climate–ice-sheet models will improve projections of long-term sea-level rise.

items.title: Community-level energy resilience under high-intensity hazard and military conflict: Frontline experience from the Ukraine war
items.summary_raw: Community-level energy resilience is an increasing policy priority as climate change and geopolitical instability intensify hazards to local energy systems. While participatory governance is recognised as a pathway to strengthening local energy-system resilience, its role under high-intensity hazards remains empirically underexamined. This study investigates how participatory governance capacities (information and awareness, inclusiveness, social cohesion and collective action, trust-building, and resource mobilisation) and structural determinants, comprising hazard exposure (contact-line exposure) and structural vulnerability (municipal relocation and municipality size), shape community-level energy resilience under high-intensity hazard. Applying ordinary least squares and multilevel models, the study analyses survey data from 145 Ukrainian municipalities collected during Russia's full-scale invasion. Municipal relocation emerges as the most robust negative predictor. Participatory governance capacities show no statistically significant independent associations beyond structural determinants across the sample; however, these findings should be contextualised within the relatively high levels and restricted variation in participatory governance capacities observed. Interaction analysis provides a more nuanced understanding: municipal relocation significantly conditions the association between social cohesion and collective action and community-level energy resilience. This…

items.title: Ironing out oxygen instability
The populist contagion: how the mainstreaming of right-wing populist rhetoric reduces public support for international aid
items.summary_raw: This article examines whether the diffusion of populist rhetoric from populist to mainstream parties reduces public support for international organisations (IOs) and multilateral aid. We argue that when mainstream parties adopt populist anti-IO rhetoric, support for aid decreases not just amongst citizens, which hold populist attitudes and support populist parties, but also among more moderate voters. To test this cueing argument, we ran a survey experiment in France, Germany, Poland, Spain, and Sweden (n = 10,513) in early 2026. Varying both the message and the messenger, the experiment reveals, first, that populist anti-IO cues, indeed, reduce support for multilateral aid. Second, the messenger matters – while populist cues from populist parties primarily affect ideologically like-minded citizens, populist rhetoric voiced by mainstream parties reduces support across the political spectrum. Third, anti-IO rhetoric specifically undermines multilateral forms of aid while leaving support for bilateral aid unchanged. In sum, our study demonstrates how the normalisation of populist rhetoric by mainstream parties jeopardises public support for multilateral responses to transboundary risks and crises. Moreover, our findings underline that the populist contestation of IOs and multilateral aid is conceptually distinct from deservingness perceptions of the global poor.

items.title: Using climax thinking to understand psychological drivers of attitudes towards two coastal climate adaptations around the hypertidal Bay of Fundy
items.summary_raw: Abstract Coastal climate adaptations are changes that tackle the challenges arising from sea level rise. Adaptations such as risk information and changes to public infrastructure have been met with some degree of public opposition. Climax thinking is an emerging framework for exploring this resistance. In this study, we used climax thinking to explore public responses to two specific coastal climate adaptation strategies: public flood risk mapping and managed dyke realignment. Using a survey administered to residents around the hypertidal Bay of Fundy, in Atlantic Canada, we found low knowledge of both. While most residents supported each, 30% expressed resistance to flood risk mapping based on real estate value concerns, and 20% expressed resistance to managed dyke realignment that might involve retreating homes or businesses. Using ordered logit models we tested the dimensions of this resistance (deploying Time Perception, Futures Consciousness, Basic Values, and Awareness of Consequences) as well as risk perceptions. Only future orientation was significant (reducing resistance) for both models, supporting its power for climate action. Other significant variables differed by the type of adaptation, showing the importance of asking about adaptation options separately, rather than climate action in general. For instance, a past focus associated with a sense of loss was shown to increase resistance for managed dyke realignment. The research suggests new areas of exploration…

items.title: School Climate and Student Engagement in Secondary School Classrooms
items.source_name: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
items.summary_raw: This study explored how school climate relates to classroom engagement among secondary school students. It examined environmental conditions that may encourage participation, barriers that may limit it, and students’ views of teacher attitudes and classroom practices. A mixed-method approach combined responses from 24 students and five guardians with interviews from five teachers.

items.title: Türkiye and Nuclear Energy: Strategic Prioritization Supported by Sustainability Consideration
items.summary_raw: In the context of Türkiye, the decision-making process concerning nuclear energy is characterised by a series of interwoven strategic considerations, including but not limited to energy security, decarbonisation, cost, technological dependence, and public acceptance. The present study employs the SWOT–AHP method, interpreted from the perspective of sustainability, to rank the strategic factors influencing Türkiye’s nuclear energy development in order of priority. A total of 12 experts from academia and public institutions evaluated a 15-factor SWOT matrix. The evaluations were then aggregated using the geometric mean. The highest priorities within the categories were identified as the existence of international co-operations such as Akkuyu NPP project (S2), insufficient technical capacity and infrastructure (W1), localisation in energy and reducing foreign dependency. (O1), and existence of active faults (T3). When category weights were set equal, O1 ranked first in the overall ranking, while social acceptance (W3) and delays in the construction of nuclear energy facilities (T1) ranked at the bottom. While the overall evaluations remained constant, the individual matrices of the majority of the experts exhibited variations. The application of bootstrap resampling revealed that the highest and lowest priorities were supported exclusively (O1 ranked first in 92% of resamples). The overall ranking demonstrated sensitivity to category weights that were not compared by the…

items.title: Work Locus of Control as a Predictor of Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence
items.summary_raw: Human Resource Development (HRD) professionals seek information on the organization's conditions that will facilitate or impede collective performance; many employee surveys focus on individual attitudes or job experiences. Based on this study, the concept of Employee-Based Organizational Performance Evaluation is developed as a diagnostic scale that is referred to the organization contains six components namely mission clarity, workforce cohesion, communication, resilience, leadership capability and accountability. The scale adds five items to an existing 22-item pool to represent accountability and four items to represent communication, building on previous organizational efficacy and perceived leadership efficacy measures. Thirty-nine employees (60% of a 65-person Midwestern U.S. service operation) completed the 31-item instrument. Exploratory analyses showed reasonably high internal consistency across the six dimensions (alpha = .758- .924) and warrant further exploration of the accountability and communication item sets. Results of an exploratory regression indicated that cohesion was uniquely related to mission. The results for this study are preliminary psychometric evidence, not a scale validation, due to the small, cross sectional, single organization sample. The instrument provides a basis for HRD practitioners and researchers to measure perceptions of HRD capability at the organizational level and to identify priorities for further instrument development and…

items.title: Decoupled ore and scrap trade networks constrain low-carbon metal supply
items.summary_raw: Abstract Global supply chains for critical metals such as aluminium and copper are increasingly exposed to sustainability and geopolitical risks under the pressure of energy transition. In this paper we compare primary (ore) and secondary (scrap) trade networks for the United States, European Union and China using multilayer network analysis. We focus on the years 2010-2023, a period that captures intensified demand for the two metals. Results identify a marked structural decoupling: around 40% of scrap-trading countries do not participate in ore trade. Further, while about 50% of ore trade links overlap with scrap networks, only some 10–15% of scrap connections overlap with ore trade. Despite strong alignment in trading partners, volumes of scrap and ore trade diverge substantially. The observed differences indicate that the two commodity streams use partly distinct international trading relationships. Major economies may compete for ore suppliers but remain interdependent in scrap trade, revealing a bifurcated system with uneven resilience. Strengthening integration between primary and secondary supply chains is therefore critical for achieving sustainable critical metal supply for the low-carbon energy transition and establishing resource-efficient metal systems.

items.title: Far-right slows energy transition
Valuing sociolinguistics for qualitative data analysis in energy community research: An exploratory study in the Navajo Nation
Advancing sustainable competitiveness in freight transport: An integrated framework with system thinking approach
items.summary_raw: Freight transport is central to economic vitality, yet a major source of congestion, emissions, and social externalities. Accordingly, the sustainability of freight transport systems is increasingly recognized as a vital element in global efforts to address climate change and improve urban livability. Building on a structured gap analysis, this paper advances the Integrated Freight Transport System Model (IFTSM) for Sustainability Competitiveness by (1) Embedding Reliability, Efficiency, and Attractiveness dimensions, (2) incorporating the Systems Thinking Approach by developing the Causal Loop Diagram, and (3) positioning the framework for future context-specific application. The framework offers a holistic structure that delineates system boundaries, defines key variables, and incorporates feedback loops to evaluate sustainability competitiveness. Phases 1 and 2 of the framework, focused on system definition and causal loop modeling, establish a conceptual foundation for future evidence-based sustainability competitiveness assessment. The proposed 12 feedback loops identify potential leverage pathways: (1) Reinvesting ROI into network quality to reduce congestion, improve safety, and cargo damage, elevating public acceptance, (2) Strengthening service quality to reinforce on-time delivery and demand, and (3) proper distribution planning to stabilize flows and capacity utilization. Once validated, the framework can be adapted to other regions through parameterization and…

items.title: Perceived economic effects and conditions associated with public acceptance of consumption-tax reform in Mogadishu, Somalia: evidence from a survey-based PLS-SEM analysis
items.summary_raw: This study examines perceptions of Somalia’s consumption-tax reform using a cross-sectional survey in Mogadishu’s Banadir region. The questionnaire items were mapped to Perceived Price and Consumption Disruption Effects (PPCD), Perceived Effects and Responses among Traders and Businesses (PETB), and Public Perceptions of Acceptance-Related Economic and Institutional Conditions (PPAEC). PPAEC captures respondents’ beliefs about factors that may influence tax acceptance; it does not measure the actual economic or institutional conditions or whether respondents personally accept the tax. The analysis used respondent-level observations, standardized reflective Mode A measurement, the PLS path-weighting procedure, and bootstrap resampling. PPCD met conventional internal-consistency and convergent-validity standards, whereas PETB and PPAEC did not meet convergent-validity requirements in the PLS solution. The descriptive proposition was supported because all PPCD item means exceeded the neutral midpoint. The PPCD-PETB path was statistically significant; however, because PETB lacked adequate measurement validity, this finding is treated as an exploratory score association and does not confirm the substantive latent-construct hypothesis. The PPCD–PPAEC score association was not statistically significant, and inadequate PPAEC measurement validity prevented a conclusive evaluation of H3. The findings do not measure actual acceptance, establish causality, or demonstrate exceptionally…

items.title: Mobilizing the seafood industry for climate action
items.summary_raw: Abstract Large seafood companies face climate-related risks across their operations, with substantial economic and financial implications. Nevertheless, corporate reporting remains limited, with nearly half of the 100 largest companies providing no climate-related disclosures. Reporting, which can be an indicator of action and priorities, has focused primarily on mitigation, with little attention to adaptation. We consider these gaps and propose four priorities to support capacity and pathways for climate-resilient seafood operations.

items.title: Green Energy Policies in Promoting Sustainable Development: A Literature Review
items.summary_raw: Green energy policies have become essential instruments for addressing climate change, environmental degradation, energy insecurity, and sustainable development challenges. This study aims to examine the role of green energy policies in promoting sustainable development by analyzing policy frameworks, implementation strategies, environmental and socioeconomic contributions, institutional challenges, and policy innovations. The study employed a literature review approach with a qualitative descriptive and analytical orientation. Relevant academic publications were identified through Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar, prioritizing peer-reviewed articles published between 2021 and 2026. Literature selection was guided by predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, while data were examined using qualitative thematic analysis and narrative synthesis. The findings indicate that renewable energy regulations, financial incentives, carbon pricing mechanisms, and investment policies contribute to emission reductions, economic development, employment opportunities, and improved energy accessibility. However, their effectiveness varies according to institutional capacity, regulatory consistency, financial accessibility, technological readiness, and stakeholder participation. Major implementation challenges include fragmented governance, inadequate financing, infrastructure limitations, technological disparities, and unequal distribution of…

items.title: Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
items.summary_raw: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system’s effective temperature with density.

items.title: Correction for Bernabé-Rubio and Watt, Caspase-8-dependent autophagy regulates neutrophil infiltration in oral squamous cell carcinoma
Hydration at the base of the mantle transition zone by ancient subductions in Asia
items.summary_raw: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine–Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol–Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth’s deep water cycle.

items.title: Potential energy landscape networks of confined vortex matter
items.summary_raw: Advances in nanoscale patterning of superconducting films [Y. L. Wang et al ., Nat. Nanotechnol. 13 , 560–565 (2018)] and the availability of submicron-sized superconducting single crystals with controlled geometry allow for the investigation of superconducting vortex matter under extreme confinement [A. K. Geim et al ., Nature 390 , 259–262 (1997)]. It has been observed in these systems that the interplay between sample geometry and vortex number results in the emergence of so-called “magic number” configurations which show unusually high stability against thermal fluctuations. However, a detailed, comprehensive theoretical study of the ground state and metastable states of confined vortex matter has not yet been developed. Here we show that the intricate properties of a system of vortices under extreme confinement can be characterized in detail by mapping the potential energy landscape of the system onto a network [J. P. K. Doye, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 , 238701 (2002)] with nodes corresponding to local potential energy minima and edges to transition states between local minima. We apply these techniques to systems featuring repelling particles/vortices confined in small containers of various geometric shapes. We demonstrate that the ground state almost always belongs to a subset of system states within the deepest network core. We find that the emergence of magic number configurations in the ground state results in a drastic decrease in the complexity of the entire network…

items.title: The efficiency of information gain by natural selection
items.summary_raw: Natural selection enriches populations for genotypes that are well adapted to their environments, accumulating information about the selective conditions in the process. Therefore, selection can be viewed as a learning process through which populations acquire information about the environment. Motoo Kimura derived a relationship between the amount of information gained by selection and a measure of the inefficiency of the selective process, known as substitution load [M. Kimura, Genet. Res. 2, 127–140 (1961)]. Due to the gradual nature of selection and the ongoing mismatch of types to the environment, a lineage that is still acquiring information has lower mean fitness than a lineage that already has it. While this has been an influential insight, we find that Kimura’s model is inconsistent with selection experiments involving Escherichia coli . To address limitations in this model and develop a more robust measure for the efficiency of selection, we turn to computational learning theory. We show that the learning-theoretic concept of regret quantifies the inefficiency of selection as a learning process in terms of relative lineage fitness. We establish bounds on the efficiency of information gain in general settings, including frequency-dependent selection and arbitrary environmental change. We experimentally validate these bounds and demonstrate that our extended theory recovers Kimura’s fundamental insight. Finally, we show that selection is an asymptotically optimal…

items.title: A sulfotyrosine motif in the human TrkB extracellular domain is required for activation by the agonist antibody ZEB85
items.summary_raw: The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling axis is a key effector of synaptic plasticity and neuroprotection. While TrkB activation is a major target to prevent neural dysfunction, stimulation with exogenous BDNF administration has not proven tractable given the unfavorable physiochemical properties of BDNF. In addition, BDNF also activates a cell death pathway by binding to the neurotrophin receptor p75. The TrkB agonist antibody ZEB85 provides an alternative route to the selective activation of TrkB. To understand the ZEB85 mechanism of action, we mapped the binding site for ZEB85 to the TrkB extracellular juxtamembrane domain and found a sulfotyrosine modification at residue 400 crucial for ZEB85 interaction and activation of TrkB signaling. We determined the structures of ZEB85 and BDNF bound to their respective binding sites on human TrkB suggesting independent sites for each ligand, despite prior evidence of direct competition. Using structure-guided BDNF- and ZEB85-binding deficient TrkB mutants, we assessed their ability to sequester ligands from full-length TrkB in cultured human neurons. We found that the BDNF binding site extends into the juxtamembrane domain of TrkB but does not require the sulfotyrosine 400 to activate TrkB. Together with biophysical analysis and AlphaFold modeling, these results explain how BDNF can displace ZEB85 from TrkB through an overlapping epitope. Our findings reveal unique features of…

items.title: A chemomechanical bifurcation landscape unifies sustained growth, length homeostasis, and regenerative collapse in axons
items.summary_raw: Axonal growth machinery is largely shared across neurons, but axons exhibit strikingly different fates depending on developmental and environmental context: sustained elongation in peripheral neurons under permissive conditions, length homeostasis in cortical neurons after target innervation, and pathological collapse into dystrophic endbulbs in injured adult central nervous system (CNS) axons. These divergent outcomes have resisted explanation by length-sensing and biomechanical models that treat long-range transport and local force generation as separate problems. We unify these phenomena through a mechanochemical model that couples bidirectional motor transport and intracellular signaling to growth-cone balance of axonal tension, actomyosin contraction, and adhesion within a single feedback loop: The lengthening axon uses its own growing transport delay to establish self-limiting mechanical feedback, as the accumulating delay reshapes signaling waveforms to progressively elevate myosin contractility against actin-driven protrusion. Two physical parameters, the transport delay and the signaling feedback strength, organize axon fate into a unified state-space landscape spanning sustained growth, length homeostasis, and pathological collapse. Reduced feedback strength weakens this self-limiting mechanical feedback by simultaneously enhancing protrusion and suppressing contractility, providing a mechanistic interpretation of axon lengthening under partial reduction of…

items.title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral–water interfaces
items.summary_raw: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral–water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes—Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations—of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct…

items.title: Ddx3x deficiency in mice impairs corticofugal motor circuits and causes motor deficits that are attenuated by early-life exercise
items.summary_raw: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of motor circuits connecting the motor cortex with the pontine nuclei. Ddx3x haploinsufficiency during development affects the dendritic arborization of corticopontine neurons. Juvenile-onset Ddx3x loss in corticopontine neurons is sufficient to induce adult motor impairments overlapping with those caused by chemogenetic disruption of corticopontine circuits. Further, Ddx3x mutant mice engage corticopontine circuits in skilled motor tasks in a sex-dependent manner. Last, Ddx3x haploinsufficient female mice undergoing a juvenile motor intervention show long-lasting specific benefits in their adult motor function. Together, these findings establish Ddx3x as an essential regulator of corticopontine neuron development and function and provide an early motor intervention to ameliorate motor outcomes in a mouse model of DDX3X haploinsufficiency.

items.title: Computation and sampling for Schubert specializations
items.summary_raw: We study a problem at the interface of enumerative algebraic geometry, algebraic combinatorics, and the statistical mechanics of vertex models with long-range interactions. We develop methods to explore the values S w ( 1 , … , 1 ) of Schubert polynomials (called principal specializations), which count reduced bumpless pipe dreams (RBPDs) with boundary permutation w ∈ S n . We exhibit counterexamples to the conjecture of Merzon and Smirnov that S w ( 1 n ) is maximized on layered permutations; the smallest such example we find is at n = 17. Despite the counterexamples, we present bounds that support a refined conjecture that the maximum of S w ( 1 n ) over all w ∈ S n grows at the same asymptotic rate as the maximum over layered permutations (found by Morales, Pak, and Panova). We implement and benchmark four recurrences for Schubert specializations: the descent formula of Macdonald, the transition formula of Lascoux–Schützenberger, the cotransition formula of Knutson, and the formula of Billey, Jockusch, and Stanley. We also explore typical random permutations drawn with probability proportional to S w ( 1 n ) , equivalently from uniformly random RBPDs. Our simulations reveal a permuton-like limit analogous to the Grothendieck setting studied by Morales, Panova, Petrov, and Yeliussizov. For sampling, we show that the standard monotone Coupling From The Past framework does not apply to RBPDs, leaving exact uniform sampling open. To bypass this, we develop an efficient Markov…

items.title: A symbiogenic merger enabled by oxygen initiated the evolution of eukaryotes
items.summary_raw: Recently, extensive genetic information about archaeal hosts at the basis of eukaryogenesis has come to light. Characterization of these first eukaryotic common ancestor (FECA) related organisms allows improved understanding of the enigmatic FECA to last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) transition. However, these gene-centered discoveries have the unfortunate side effect of entrenching erroneous ideas about early eukaryotic evolution. This is apparent in the two-Domain vision of life, with eukaryotes seen as specialized Asgard archaea, while underestimating the contribution of the endosymbiont to eukaryogenesis. Establishment of the alpha-proteobacterium as the future mitochondrion is treated as one of many such endosymbiotic occurrences, ignoring its unique evolutionary position. I will marshal evidence for symbiogenic mechanisms involved in the FECA to LECA transition, with a key role for the endosymbiont’s electron transport chain and its acceptor molecular oxygen, especially in the incarnation of reactive oxygen species occurring in the host cytoplasm. We should overcome overestimating gene determinism, while not sufficiently allowing for effects of biological hierarchies, emergent properties, and chance. Many eukaryotic properties are best understood by envisaging the crucial uptake of the future mitochondrion as a merger instead of an acquisition. This merger is characterized by a new kind of elaborate cellular entity emerging as a result of rapid coevolution…

items.title: Intrinsic function of leptin receptor–regulated endothelial PD-L1
items.summary_raw: Programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an immune checkpoint protein expressed in vascular endothelial cells (ECs). In contrast to cancer, our understanding of endothelial PD-L1 in relation to metabolic syndromes and its vascular complications is less studied. For example, its regulation and intrinsic function remain unclear. Here, we showed that endothelial PD-L1 is regulated by leptin receptor signaling in male mice. In particular, endothelial PD-L1 expression is affected by leptin resistance. A lack of leptin receptors leads to PD-L1 downregulation in vascular ECs via posttranslational degradation. To understand the fundamental roles of endothelial PD-L1, RNA interference and selective knockout are employed in human endothelium and animals, respectively. Silencing or deleting endothelial PD-L1 expression delays cell cycle progression and proliferation due to rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inactivation. In obesity, endothelial PD-L1 deficiency impairs the EC turnover and worsens the vascular function. Overall, we provide an insight into how endothelial PD-L1 contributes to vascular homeostasis, suggesting its pathophysiological importance in maintaining cellular turnover.

items.title: The ABCD hypothesis
items.summary_raw: If α and β are cardinals, then the cardinal exponentiation α β is the set of all functions from α into β . The ABCD hypothesis is the statement that for all infinite cardinals α ≤ β and γ ≤ δ , | α β | ≤ | γ δ | if and only if α ≤ γ and β ≤ δ . The Axiom of Determinacy, AD, states that every two-player infinite game on ω has a winning strategy for one of the two players. Let Θ be the supremum of the ordinals onto which R surjects. This paper will show that if AD holds and V = L ( R ) , then the ABCD hypothesis holds below Θ .

items.title: In eastern Montana, a new oil pipeline comes with perils and a potential payday
items.summary_raw: Jerry Arnold stands in a patch of cleared land, his combine idling behind him. To the west, acres of freshly cut grain reveal rolling hills, and to the east, 3-foot stalks of wheat pulse in the wind. Arnold’s sweat-stained baseball cap is coated with fine golden dust after a day of harvesting at his farm near Opheim, Montana, a town with a population of 72 near the Canada border. Last year’s warm, dry winter hit Arnold’s unirrigated farm hard. Record-low snowpack left moisture in short supply, stunting crops’ growth. But he could soon see some financial relief. Arnold is one of nearly 300 Montana landowners in the path of a proposed pipeline that would traverse nine counties in eastern Montana and an expanse of eastern Wyoming. “We’re coming off of two, three bad years,” Arnold said, “and that’s going to be a good-size check.” Wyoming-based Bridger Pipeline LLC plans to build a 650-mile pipeline to move tar sands oil — a dense mix of sand, clay, water, and a molasses-like form of petroleum that generates about 20 percent more greenhouse gas emissions compared to conventional crude. The route would connect to an existing Canadian pipeline and run through Montana to an oil refinery hub and trading center in Guernsey, Wyoming. The company has said it plans to break ground within a year . This spring, President Donald Trump granted the project a presidential permit authorizing it to cross the Canadian border. items.title: The new Cold War comes to Kodiak
items.summary_raw: Last August, Christine Burton got an unexpected call from her sister, an employee at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska. The state-owned facility was about to conduct an unannounced test launch of what was likely a hypersonic missile and would be closing the only road that runs from the center of town to the site. Burton knew the drill. She and her husband, Buck, owned and operated a 140-acre bison ranch that abuts the Spaceport and, for the last couple of years, had had to deal with the many disruptions that came with it: road closures, accidents — at least five rockets have exploded or malfunctioned during takeoff, releasing debris and toxic material into the surrounding environment — and last-minute changes for clients hunting game on their land. Plus, their home is on the same two-lane road to the facility. When the road is shut down, the Burtons and their six children are effectively stranded. Usually, they’d get a couple of days’ notice, allowing them time to make any necessary arrangements. But this time there was no such buffer. Her sister had called to let her know that the road would be closed that evening for the test launch, so Burton left work early and drove home. Then, about a half hour later, she observed an unmarked security vehicle blocking her driveway. This, more than anything, she found infuriating.
