items.title: Public support for net-zero climate policy packages under political party cues
items.summary_raw: Despite widespread climate change mitigation pledges, effective policy implementation faces persistent political opposition. This study investigates how political party cues shape public support for multi-sectoral climate policy mixes, and whether distinct audience segments and levels of issue salience moderate these effects. We conducted a conjoint experiment with 1,201 Canadian adults who evaluated policy packages varying across regulations and support policies for transportation and housing, and party endorsements. Latent class analysis identified five distinct audience segments. Three main findings emerged. First, party cues were more influential than the contents of proposed policy packages. Second, despite heterogeneity across segments, rejection of government inaction and broad support for ‘bridge policies’ revealed unexpected consensus. Third, issue salience provided minimal insulation against party cue effects. Results suggest that in Canada’s polarized context, political messenger strategy may prove as consequential as policy design for building public support.

items.title: From Iran–Israel Conflict Feeds to Sustainable Energy Transition Support
items.source_name: East Asian Journal of Multidisciplinary Research
items.summary_raw: This study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior to resolve empirical anomalies regarding media effects by examining how social media exposure to the Iran–Israel conflict and information literacy shape university students' attitudes toward supporting sustainable energy transition amid Indonesia's 2026 fuel subsidy restrictions. Analyzing PLS-SEM data from 427 undergraduate students across five state universities in Malang City, the findings reveal that under high-stakes macro-geopolitical shocks, both conflict exposure and information literacy transcend routine non-significant effects to exert statistically significant positive impacts (R2 = 0.075). This offers a novel theoretical framework showing how global crises activate youth policy support, highlighting key digital communication strategies for national energy security.

items.title: The public opinion crisis surrounding I Am What I Am : When ACGN nationalist discourse encounters identity backlash
items.summary_raw: In creative practices and academic research, Chinese animation has maintained an intrinsic connection with nationalism. This study examines the operational mechanisms of animation, comics, games, and novels (ACGN) nationalism in Chinese animation, focusing on I Am What I Am 雄狮少年. This animated film series, centring on lion dance and Chinese martial arts, has received support from official institutions but generated a public opinion crisis because of its unconventional artistic style, character designs, and thematic expressions. This article argues that the national identity of Chinese animation is no longer a unidirectional self-definition but instead requires three levels of validation: recognition by official discourse, conscious construction by creators, and cultural identification by audiences. The last, and third, is critical as audiences not only determine commercial returns but also are active participants in the nationalist discourse. Since ACGN audiences are aesthetically conservative and culturally perceptive, innovation in animated filmmaking leads to market risks and public controversy.

items.title: The carbon divide: exploring economic and cultural dimensions of climate change attitudes and climate policy support in the Netherlands
items.summary_raw: While climate attitudes and policy have become polarized in public debate, it remains unclear how climate attitudes map onto the economic and cultural dimensions of political conflict or form a separate dimension. By examining a wide range of climate attitudes (Study 1) and using a vignette experiment on climate policy designs (Study 2), this study further disentangles the ideological entanglement of climate attitudes. The findings show that while the cultural dimension is substantially related to all climate attitudes, the economic dimension is particularly relevant for more concrete climate concerns. Yet, climate attitudes could not be fully captured by these dimensions and thus appear to form a partially distinct dimension. Furthermore, we show that although the economic redistributive effects of climate policies can be influenced by policy design choices, support for different designs does not seem to differ across cultural or economic positions.

items.title: Carbon emissions trading and high-quality agricultural development in China: evidence from staggered adoption
items.summary_raw: China’s Carbon Emissions Trading (CET) pilots may affect agriculture through input costs, investment, technology adoption, and environmental governance. Using provincial data for 2007–2020, this study estimates cohort-time effects of CET exposure on High-Quality Agricultural Development (HQAD), an index covering innovation, coordination, greening, openness, and sharing. The analysis covers 30 province-level regions and three adoption cohorts defined by trading commencement in 2013, 2014, and 2016. The five-year average treatment effect on the treated is 0.02091 HQAD index units (standard error 0.00873; 95% confidence interval [0.00380−0.03802]), indicating a positive average response over the launch year and the following four years. In the candidate-channel regressions, CET exposure is positively associated with environmental regulation intensity in all three samples, with 95% confidence intervals above zero. The CET coefficients for agricultural energy total factor productivity (AETFP) are positive in both samples, with intervals that include zero. All five intermediate-outcome coefficients in the next-year HQAD equations have intervals that include zero. These coefficients describe conditional associations. Separate simulation benchmarks compare first-difference Double Machine Learning (DML) specifications, with coefficients ranging from 0.00628 to 0.01066 across nuisance learners.

items.title: Current status and challenges of food biotechnology in Africa
items.summary_raw: Food biotechnology has the potential to solve many of Africa’s agricultural problems. However, the current status of this technology and the challenges preventing its widespread adoption are not well understood. Progress is hindered by a substantial lack of long-term, region-specific field data on the ecological and socio-economic impacts of genetically modified crops in different African agro-ecological zones. Such data is crucial for moving beyond generalised concerns and informing evidence-based policy. To address this issue, this review analysed peer-reviewed journal articles, reports and other relevant documents rigorously selected from Google Scholar, Web of Science and Scopus. The review outlines the current situation and the main obstacles to implementing food biotechnology in Africa, as well as its potential for improvement. The main barriers to widespread acceptance were found to be misinformation and concerns about the safety, environmental impact and ethical implications of genetically modified crops. These concerns can result in policy restrictions and unfavourable public perceptions. This study recommends improving technology transfer and providing small-scale farmers with access to biotech products. This would provide African governments, policymakers, stakeholders, and farmers with the necessary information to increase their acceptance of food biotechnology, ultimately improving food availability.

items.title: Monopolising the green transition: China's structural dominance and selective weaponisation of critical raw materials in Europe
items.summary_raw: Europe's ambitious energy transition risks replacing strategic dependence on Russian fossil fuels with dependence on Chinese critical raw materials. While concerns over mineral weaponisation are widespread, empirical assessments of China's actual supply-chain leverage remain underexplored. Bridging this gap, this article applies a disciplined interpretative case study design and realist theory to construct an analytical model to assess whether Beijing weaponises its position vis-à-vis the EU. It traces China's strategic behaviour between 2013 and 2025 across four commodities crucial for renewable technologies: gallium, magnesium, rare earth elements, and vanadium. The analysis reveals that Beijing has systematically consolidated state control over these sectors. Rare earth elements and vanadium pose the highest risk of weaponisation due to export restrictions, investment barriers, and stockpiling, whereas magnesium exhibits the fewest strategic indicators. Furthermore, although China has deployed targeted export bans against the United States, it has exercised strategic restraint toward Europe. The study concludes that while the structural capacity for coercion is deeply embedded in China's mineral governance, overt weaponisation remains highly selective, suggesting that dependent nations must prioritise diversification in the most vulnerable supply chains.

items.title: Climate change impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem-based adaptation mechanisms in Azerbaijan
items.source_name: Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research
items.summary_raw: Climate change is altering ecosystems, species distributions and the services that support human well-being, while habitat loss and unsustainable resource use intensify ecological vulnerability. This narrative review examines the major pathways through which warming, hydrological change and extreme events affect biodiversity and identifies adaptation mechanisms relevant to Azerbaijan. The paper synthesizes authoritative global assessments, peer-reviewed literature and selected national policy documents, with emphasis on forests, mountain ecosystems, freshwater habitats, agricultural landscapes and nature-based solutions. The reviewed evidence links climate stress to habitat modification, range shifts, altered seasonal processes, water scarcity and increasing pressure on ecosystem services, although local impacts depend on land use, exposure and species-specific sensitivity. Ecosystem-based adaptation offers opportunities through habitat restoration, ecological connectivity, water and soil conservation, sustainable forestry and biodiversity-sensitive land management. These measures require careful ecological design because poorly located tree planting or other single-purpose interventions may create trade-offs for water resources and native species. For Azerbaijan, integrating biodiversity monitoring into climate planning, aligning adaptation investments with watershed-scale risk, and involving local communities are practical priorities. The review concludes that protecting…

items.title: Green hydrogen and alternative fuels for climate mitigation: a cross-sectoral techno-economic and deployment perspective
items.summary_raw: Green hydrogen and its low-carbon derivatives are increasingly considered for decarbonising sectors in which direct electrification is technically constrained or cannot replace a required molecular feedstock. This review examines the technical, techno-economic, environmental, infrastructure, and deployment conditions that determine where green hydrogen and hydrogen-derived alternative fuels can provide effective climate-mitigation pathways across major end-use sectors. Global hydrogen demand reached approximately 100 Mt in 2024, while low-emissions hydrogen accounted for less than 1% of supply. Announced projects could provide approximately 37 Mtpa by 2030, yet only about 4.2 Mtpa has reached operation or final investment decision, indicating a substantial project-bankability gap. The synthesis shows that electricity cost, utilisation, offtake certainty, infrastructure, regulatory eligibility, renewable-resource availability, and water management govern hydrogen deployment. Conversion to ammonia, methanol, and synthetic hydrocarbons introduces additional energy losses but can provide storage, transport, and infrastructure advantages in shipping and aviation.

items.title: Women at the Core of Climate-Smart Agriculture: Advancing Equity and Food Security through Empowerment
items.source_name: Journal of Agricultural Policy and Transformation
items.summary_raw: Climate volatility threatens global food security, particularly in developing nations where female farmers face severe resource barriers. This narrative review synthesizes empirical research published between 2010 and 2026 to evaluate women’s empowerment, climate-smart agricultural adoption, and household food security. Applying structured narrative frameworks, 44 academic studies and policy reports were synthesized across four major academic databases. The selected literature was analyzed using Feminist Political Ecology and the Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index conceptual frameworks. Findings reveal that conventional technical adaptation programs often fail by ignoring local power dynamics and increasing female unpaid care burdens. In contrast, gender-responsive interventions addressing land tenure, credit constraints, and information gaps generate strong economic benefits. Securing equal access to essential productive assets directly increases agricultural yields for female farmers. This productivity gain expands household dietary diversity, reduces child stunting, and strengthens climate shock absorption. Labor-saving equipment and solar micro-irrigation reduce drudgery while improving seasonal farm earnings. However, national climate policies often ignore gender metrics, lack gender-disaggregated data, and risk male control over profitable practices. Achieving sustainable food security requires moving from gender-neutral programs toward gender-transformative…

From Maximizing to Minimizing Responsibility: A Comparative Analysis of Facebook’s Election Integrity Framing in News Media and the Meta Newsroom
items.summary_raw: Over the past decade, Facebook has become known for its dangerously flawed approach to election integrity issues. Yet few studies have examined how Meta frames Facebook’s role in election integrity and how these frames are taken up in public discourse. We use qualitative textual analysis to compare framings of Facebook’s political influence between Meta’s Newsroom blog and major American newspapers during the 2020 and 2024 U.S. presidential elections. Findings suggest that the Newsroom blog and newspapers adopted a techno-solutionist imaginary that positions Facebook as the most potent solution for digital threats to democracy. Over time, the framing mechanisms supporting this imaginary shifted from maximizing Meta’s responsibility for election integrity issues to minimizing it. We consider how these frames support the company’s efforts to avoid government regulation and contextualize Meta’s drastic content moderation changes in early 2025.

items.title: Exploring the role of frame analysis in promoting inclusive climate action: Insights from the GALLANT project
items.summary_raw: Abstract The context of this article is the “Glasgow as a Living Laboratory, Accelerating Novel Transformation” (GALLANT) project (2022–2028), a collaborative initiative that brings together researchers, community organisations and residents to explore how climate change, environmental degradation and environmental enhancement are experienced and made sense of in everyday urban contexts. The research presented here employed frame analysis, conceptualised by Erving Goffman in the 1970s, to examine community perceptions of urban climate resilience and adaptation. Guided by participatory action research (PAR), transdisciplinary principles and an understanding of learning cities as ongoing processes of lifelong learning and participatory governance rather than fixed models, the authors explore how community environmental and social relations, experiences, values and priorities are negotiated in relation to climate change and biodiversity loss. Focusing on community-generated frames, the article offers a nuanced view of learning for climate action as a collective endeavour. It highlights diverse community perspectives on climate adaptation and emphasises the importance of place-based and participatory methods, including photovoice, for surfacing these perspectives. Through a photo-elicitation analytical lens, four themes emerge: just energy transition; a sharing city; nature-based solutions; and community activities. The study contributes to debates on inclusive climate action…

items.title: Purpose, scale and power: expanding the role of community benefits for the energy transition
items.summary_raw: The energy transition is neither proceeding as rapidly, nor as widely, as required to meet global climate policy goals. Moreover, the energy transition is under pressure due to rising far right political movements which frame the economic shifts required as a threat to livelihoods. One strategy for generating support for renewable energy development has been the distribution of “benefits” by project proponents. In this critical review, we explore the literature on benefit sharing in distinct contexts: energy projects, urban infrastructure and the extractive industry. Reading the literature through a theoretical lens that centres community engagement, power relations and social provisioning economic theory, we argue that prevailing approaches to benefit sharing for the energy transition are too narrow. We propose three changes that constitute a new point of departure for benefit sharing in the energy transition. First, we expand the scale of benefit sharing from project to recognise that the scale of the energy transition impacts not only the immediate and local area but the economy as a whole. This demands that we query not only the scale, but also the objective of benefit sharing. Existing benefit sharing practice often adopts a compensatory aim. We argue instead that the purpose of benefit sharing, should be broad-based, redistributive and prioritise agency for community parties. This reorientation demands that “the community” be actively and consciously constructed…

items.title: Climate change, agricultural productivity, and food security: Evidence from climate-vulnerable economies
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Climate change is increasingly recognised as one of the principal threats to agricultural systems and to the food security of vulnerable populations. This article synthesises the empirical evidence on how rising temperatures, shifting precipitation patterns, and more frequent extreme events affect agricultural productivity and the four dimensions of food security (availability, access, utilization, and stability) in climate-vulnerable economies, with particular attention to Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Central Asia. Drawing on a structured narrative review of crop-model, panel-econometric, and household-level studies, the paper identifies the main transmission channels from climate shocks to food insecurity and evaluates the effectiveness of adaptation strategies. The evidence indicates that warming has already slowed agricultural productivity growth, that impacts are strongly non-linear and unevenly distributed, and that low-income economies with rain-fed agriculture, limited irrigation, and weak institutions face the largest losses. Adaptation measures such as climate-resilient crop varieties, efficient water management, crop diversification, and climate-risk insurance can offset a substantial share of projected damages, but only when supported by finance, extension services, and stable policy environments. The article concludes with policy recommendations and priorities for future research.

items.title: Towards European hydrogen market design: Perspectives from transmission system operators
items.summary_raw: Despite hydrogen being central to Europe’s decarbonisation strategy, only a small share of renewable hydrogen projects have reached final investment decision. A key barrier is uncertainty about how future hydrogen markets will be designed and operated, particularly under Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin requirements. This study investigates the extent to which future hydrogen market design can be adapted from existing natural gas markets, and the challenges it must address. The analysis was based on a survey on future hydrogen market design targeting European gas transmission system operators, the stakeholder group responsible for operating the network and implementing the Network Codes. The survey provided an assessment of mechanism transferability and identified challenges for the early development of the hydrogen market. Core market design principles and trading frameworks are broadly transferable from natural gas markets, such as entry-exit systems and virtual trading points. Capacity allocation requires targeted adaptation to improve coupling with electricity markets. Tariffs require adaptation through intertemporal cost allocation, distributing infrastructure costs over time to protect early adopters. Balancing regimes should be revisited to reflect hydrogen’s physical characteristics and different linepack flexibility uses. Key challenges for early hydrogen markets include: temporal mismatches between variable renewable supply and expected relatively stable…

items.title: Drought in the cloud: recognizing, framing, and contesting drought as a climate risk in Dutch social media discussions
items.summary_raw: Abstract Public debate plays an important role in shaping responses to climate-related hazards such as drought. While considerable attention has been given to the physical dimensions of drought, less is known about how public debate shapes societal understanding of drought. This study examines how drought became socially recognized, framed and contested on social media in the Netherlands, a country traditionally more familiar with flood than drought management. Using a combination of social network analysis and AI-assisted classification of Dutch tweets posted between 2015 and 2022, we tracked the evolution of drought-related online communities and how they discuss and frame drought. The results show a shift from discussions of drought as a distant international issue towards a national challenge following the severe Dutch drought of 2018. As drought impacts became increasingly visible, discussions expanded beyond reporting impacts to include debates on climate change, agriculture, nature conservation and water governance. Competing frames emerged around responsibility for drought impacts and competing water demands between nature and agriculture. Some communities emphasized the role of historical land and water management practices in exacerbating drought vulnerability, while several climate-sceptical communities questioned the attribution of drought to climate change. In parts of the discussion, farmers were also portrayed primarily as victims rather than contributors to…

items.title: Unmanagement Education for the Age of Climate Crisis
items.summary_raw: Abstract This paper examines how embodied, situated and relational experiences outside‐the‐classroom can open space for epistemic dislocations in Management Education under conditions of ecological crisis. Drawing on a qualitative pedagogical experience in a sustainability course in Brazil, informed by Design‐Based Research—whose assumptions of control, design and predictability we critically question–we explore conditions under which radical imaginaries may emerge through such experiences. Students engaged in encounters with human and non‐human others that generated discomfort and tension with habitual ways of knowing, opening possibilities for the emergence of (dis)enchanted imaginaries of Nature and (de)colonial imaginaries. These dynamics were intensified through situated and embodiment engagements, which at times gave rise to epistemic dislocations, or moments in which established ways of knowing lose their capacity to organize experience as alternative imaginaries become available. Those dislocations created temporary openings for participants to re‐examine their understandings of Nature, coloniality and socio‐ecological relations, remaining susceptible to reabsorption into dominant managerial frames. We contribute to climate‐oriented pedagogy by introducing Unmanagement Education, a reflexive pedagogical approach grounded in non‐mastery, embodiment and situated relationality, that may unsettle instituted imaginaries, opening space for epistemic dislocations to emerge…

items.title: Industrial Solid Wastes Recycling from Steel and Power Sectors Delivers Climate and Net Societal Benefits
items.summary_raw: Abstract Sectoral decarbonization can substantially reshape the quantity and composition of industrial solid waste and its associated resource recovery potential, yet how these changes evolve along decarbonization pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a sectoral transition framework linking future waste generation, recycling technologies, life cycle environmental impacts, and societal benefits. We focus on the steel and power sectors, which represent major industrial solid waste sources and distinct decarbonization pathways across six major producing regions from 2025 to 2050. By 2050, steel sector wastes remain at 0.61–0.78 Gt, whereas power sector wastes decline from 1.11 Gt in 2025 to 0.17–0.50 Gt. Under four scenarios, cumulative mitigation ranges from 25.68 to 53.39 Gt CO2-eq, with discounted net societal benefits of USD 11.24–23.81 trillion. Steel sector benefits are sensitive to recycling technology shares, whereas power sector benefits are more strongly shaped by transition-driven changes in the waste generation and composition. These findings highlight the importance of integrating evolving waste flows and technology choices into long-term decarbonization and circular economy strategies.

items.title: A novel Solar-Driven Molten-Salt methane pyrolysis system with direct Particle-to-Reactor-Wall heat Transfer: Design and Techno-Economic assessment
items.summary_raw: This study proposes a solar-driven methane pyrolysis system in which a particle-based concentrating solar power (CSP) plant supplies heat directly to an array of molten-salt (MnCl 2 –KCl) bubble-column reactors through the reactor wall, without an intermediate heat-transfer fluid or electric heating step. An hourly-resolved CSP model over a full year, comprising a heliostat field, a free-falling particle receiver, and two-bin thermal energy storage, is coupled to a reactor model that includes reaction kinetics, bubble hydrodynamics, particle-to-salt heat transfer, and equipment sizing. The integrated plant is assessed through a techno-economic analysis for a site in Daggett, California. At the baseline design (hot and cold particle temperatures of 1100 and 950 °C, 14 h of storage), the bulk salt temperature is 936 °C, the plant reaches a capacity factor of 69% and a single-pass methane conversion of 45%, and it produces about 6700 t/yr of hydrogen at a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH 2 ) of $3.87/kg without carbon credit and $3.52/kg with credit for the co-produced carbon. Raising the reactor temperature increases the cost of solar heat but lowers LCOH 2 through faster kinetics and fewer reactor modules, so the CSP and reactor subsystems must be designed jointly. Natural gas accounts for about 54% of LCOH 2 , and the particle-to-wall heat transfer coefficient is the most influential design parameter. At an assumed hydrogen price of $4/kg, the project has a positive 30-year…

items.title: Media Framing of Student Violence Against Teachers in Indonesia: Criminalization of Discipline and Erosion of Pedagogical Authority
items.summary_raw: Student violence against teachers in Indonesia has emerged as a documented institutional concern, yet the role of media framing in actively constructing public understanding of these incidents remains underexplored. This study examines how detikNews, Indonesia’s most widely accessed news portal, frames student violence against teachers across 14 high-profile cases (2017–2025). Each case was systematically coded using Entman’s (1993) four framing functions — problem definition, causal attribution, moral evaluation, and treatment recommendation — to identify recurring narrative patterns. Three dominant master frames were identified: Criminalization of Pedagogical Discipline, in which routine disciplinary acts are constructed as criminal rights violations; Symbolic Violence and the Viral Motive, in which classroom confrontations are staged for digital audiences; and Fatal and Collective Aggression, in which lethal and mob-based violence is framed as institutional crisis. Across all three frames, coverage consistently displaces school conflict into the legal-criminal domain and supplies justification scripts — including denial of the teacher’s victim status — that reduce perpetrator accountability. These findings call for pedagogical journalism guidelines in media reporting and Lex Specialis legal protections for educators in Indonesian education policy.

Multiple regression models and alternative proxies are used to test the robustness of results. Findings The results show that AC independence, gender diversity and expertise are associated with higher physical- and transition-risk disclosure, consistent with stronger monitoring and closer review of climate-related narratives in 10-K filings. Longer committee tenure is linked to lower disclosure, suggesting that familiarity with management may soften scrutiny over time. The presence of an AC is also associated with higher disclosure. These results are stronger in carbon-intensive sectors and remain stable across multiple robustness tests. Defects in components of the primary cilium result in an array of developmental syndromes called ciliopathies. items.title: Defining and measuring proximity to criticality based on univariate time series
items.summary_raw: Diverse social, engineered, and biological systems are made up of multiple interacting dynamical components; to work properly, certain components must be carefully regulated so that their dynamics avoid instability. However, many desirable properties, like optimized computation and control, emerge close to the tipping point between stability and instability, i.e., near criticality. Claims that such dynamical systems operate near criticality have been controversial because it is difficult to assess proximity to criticality when control parameters are unknown, hard to manipulate experimentally, and fluctuating in response to changing environmental or internal conditions. Moreover, observations of system dynamics are often limited to time series measurements of one or a few components. Here we develop a temporal renormalization group theory for defining criticality for univariate time series models and an information theoretic definition of proximity to criticality that is independent of model parameterization. We apply this theory to order-n autoregressive models resulting in a data-analytic strategy for time-resolved estimates of proximity to criticality based on measured univariate time series. After benchmarking our approach on diverse ground-truth cases, we apply it to recordings of spiking activity in the mammalian brain. Our estimate of proximity to criticality predicts behavior and suggests that brain dynamics shift closer to criticality during wakefulness and shift…

items.title: A glycan superbinder reveals polysialylated-CD56 as a precision biomarker for pancreatic cancer
items.summary_raw: Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies, largely due to the lack of reliable biomarkers for early detection. Aberrant glycosylation presents a promising source of diagnostic signatures, yet polysialic acid (polySia), a distinctive glycan, has remained underexplored, primarily owing to limitations in detection methods and recognition tools. Here, we report the development of a polySia “superbinder,” a nanoscale molecularly imprinted polymer (nanoMIP) that exhibits superior specificity and affinity for polySia over monoclonal antibodies, enabling precise recognition and quantification of this glycan. Leveraging this superbinder, we uncover a previously unrecognized association between polySia and pancreatic cancer and establish polysialylated CD56 (polySia-CD56) as a specific and robust biomarker. PolySia-CD56 outperforms multiple previously reported pancreatic cancer biomarkers, including the clinical standard carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). Notably, its expression pattern is complementary to that of CA19-9, and the combined use of both biomarkers significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy to 94.1%, effectively addressing the limitation of CA19-9 in detecting CA19-9-negative patients. Together, this study not only identifies polySia-CD56 as a precise biomarker for pancreatic cancer but also highlights the potential of antiglycan nanoMIPs as transformative reagents for decoding glycosylated targets and advancing clinical translation.

items.title: Functional redundancy between atypical CDKs reveals a vulnerability in hepatocellular carcinoma
items.summary_raw: The atypical cyclin-dependent kinase subfamily (CDK14–18) encompasses five related proteins with unclear function, and for which individual depletion has not demonstrated sustained therapeutic relevance. We report here that CDK16 and CDK18 compensate each other and liver cancer cells are sensitive to the concomitant inactivation of both kinases, resulting in persistent defects in DNA repair and subsequent cell death. These effects are linked to a role of CDK16/18 in regulating nucleocytoplasmatic transport through phosphorylation of nuclear pore complex components, including NUP35. Genetic ablation of Cdk16 and Cdk18 in established liver tumors driven by MYC and beta-catenin oncogenes triggers DNA damage in cancer cells without affecting adjacent normal tissue, ultimately leading to tumor regression. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for the development of CDK16–18 inhibitors—likely targeting multiple subfamily members due to their structural similarity—as a strategy against aggressive cancers, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, where effective treatment options remain limited.

items.title: Multiplex mapping of social roles in isolated Honduran village networks
items.summary_raw: Human social networks involve multiple kinds of relationships—such as friendship, health support, and economic exchange—that serve different functions and compete for limited time and resources. Here, we deploy a compositional framework to infer functional roles in directed multiplex networks. We distinguish outgoing ties that reflect social behavior of individuals’ allocation of social effort from incoming ties that capture structural dependence, or social appeal. The method accounts for heterogeneity in individual activity levels and layer density across relational domains. Applying this approach to multiplex sociocentric network data from 23,378 individuals across 176 rural Honduran villages, we uncover well-defined role structures spanning friendship, health-related support, and economic interactions. We find a pronounced asymmetry: behavioral (outgoing) roles exhibit weaker demographic association but stronger geographic organization than incoming roles. This is consistent with shared local environments at the village-wide level shaping social action. In contrast, structural (incoming) roles show more pronounced life-course transitions and socioeconomic differentiation, with little geographic association. Taken together, these patterns reveal a systematic difference in how social behavior and social appeal are organized in multiplex social systems. This approach illustrates a general framework for studying social roles, inequality, and life-course dynamics in complex…

items.title: Profile of Barbara Sherwood Lollar
items.summary_raw: In a laboratory nearly 2.4 kilometers under the Canadian Shield, geochemist Barbara Sherwood Lollar has tracked the sustained release of enough hydrogen gas from Earth’s crust to produce 4.7 million kilowatt-hours of energy per year. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2022, Sherwood Lollar revisited the Kidd Creek Mine in Ontario, Canada where, in 2013, her explorations found that waters flowing from deep fractures were 1.6 billion years old. Reported in her Inaugural Article, the findings, aided by studies of noble gases in the samples, pushed the age of Earth’s oldest waters back by hundreds of millions of years.

items.title: Quantifying ancient architecture: Stone-level machine learning reveals architectural variation and settlement growth at Shivta
items.summary_raw: Built environments provide durable evidence for how ancient settlements were organized, expanded, and transformed over time. Yet quantitative approaches to documenting architectural variability are generally labor-intensive, limited to individual structures, or dependent on aggregate volumetric estimates. We present a scalable, machine-learning-based framework that shifts the unit of analysis to the individual building stone and combines two complementary datasets: low-altitude drone imagery of surface remains and close-range photographs of standing walls. Applied to the Late Antique settlement of Shivta in the Negev Desert, the method automatically digitized approximately 235,000 surface stones and 12,000 stones in 604 walls, quantifying stone size, shape regularity, and masonry arrangement across walls, households, insulae, and the settlement as a whole. Higher masonry scores cluster around churches and parts of the settlement boundary, while the spatial distribution of masonry variation reveals a previously unidentified earlier boundary and provides evidence for outward expansion from a southern core. Combined with architectural sequencing, these patterns indicate the use of larger and more regularly shaped stones during Shivta’s principal phase of growth. The framework combines analytical flexibility with demonstrated robustness, supporting broader application across diverse stone-built archaeological contexts while complementing architectural energetics and enabling…

items.title: Orexin and pupillary modulation for hunger control
items.summary_raw: Fasting-based interventions improve metabolic health and are also explored as adjuncts in other clinical settings, but hunger remains a barrier to adherence. Fasting activates AgRP/NPY neurons (ANs), a hunger-promoting population whose inhibition reduces eating in hungry animals. Here we identify hypocretin/orexin neurons (HONs), classically associated with arousal, as rapid suppressors of AN activity. HON ablation increased AN population activity, whereas HON optostimulation rapidly suppressed it. Combined recordings of AN activity and pupil size—a direct arousal metric not previously linked to AN dynamics—revealed that HONs contributed to pupil dilation-associated AN suppression. In fasted mice, sensory stimulation rapidly recruited this pupil-HON pathway, and suppressed AN activity and eating. These findings reveal an arousal–hunger pathway through which self-initiated pupil dilations, or dilations driven by salient environmental events, interrupt fasting-induced hunger signals. They also suggest a framework for noninvasive, sensory-, and pupillometry-guided approaches to hunger control during fasting.

Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory
items.summary_raw: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions. Through genetic manipulations, we show that reducing hippocampal Kcr levels impairs memory, while increasing Kcr levels by means of crotonate administration enhances long-term memory. Single-nuclei transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses reveal that crotonate facilitates activation of genes regulating glutamate signaling. Cell–cell communication analysis further suggests a strengthening of glutamatergic signaling within hippocampal excitatory neurons following crotonate administration. Real-time fluorescence imaging with genetically encoded sensors functionally validates our multiomics and computational findings—demonstrating the role of Kcr in regulating presynaptic glutamate release and neuronal activity. In summary, our findings elucidate a key mechanism underlying long-term memory consolidation and excitatory neurotransmission, linking epigenetic events to synaptic…

items.title: DCAF6 reprograms TGF-β responses through TRIM33 destruction
items.summary_raw: TGF-β signaling plays a pivotal role in regulating numerous cellular processes, primarily through the Smad-dependent pathway. Disruptions of the pathway are associated with developmental disorders and life-threatening diseases, such as cancer. It has been reported that TRIM33 inactivates Smad4 signaling and also drives its own signaling responses. However, the mechanism controlling TRIM33 activity has remained unclear. In this study, we identify DCAF6 as a previously unrecognized ubiquitin ligase for TRIM33. DCAF6 targets TRIM33 at Lys850 for ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, thus abolishing TRIM33-mediated mono-ubiquitination of Smad4. As such, DCAF6 induces dual consequences: it enhances Smad4-dependent transcriptional and growth inhibitory responses, while simultaneously eliminating TRIM33-dependent developmental responses. Conversely, DCAF6 knockout suppresses Smad4-dependent responses while amplifying TRIM33-dependent responses. Therefore, DCAF6 operates as a critical regulator in the balance of TGF-β signaling between the Smad4 and TRIM33 pathways. These insights deepen our understanding of the dynamics and fate control of TGF-β signaling and may open avenues for therapeutic approaches targeting TGF-β in diseases.

items.title: Cooperative nature of residue interactions in biomolecular condensates
items.summary_raw: Cooperativity of residue interactions is prevalent in proteins and plays an essential role in protein folding. However, whether cooperativity exists in intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their assembled biomolecular condensates remains elusive. Here, we reveal the presence of residue interaction cooperativity in various IDP condensates using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations. In all these condensates, cooperative residue interactions manifest as packing between finite residue motifs (3 to 5 residues) with lifetimes three orders of magnitude longer than residue contacts. Notably, these higher-order interactions (HOIs) exhibit a significant nonadditive free energy, which originates from a local low-dielectric environment. The underlying sequence patterns like “Y-X-Q”, “D-X-R”, and “S-Y-X” are identified. Furthermore, HOIs dominate the cohesive energy of IDPs and condensates can be treated as HOI-crosslinked networks. This model can successfully reproduce experimental results of condensate physical properties, including saturation concentration, viscoelasticity, and interfacial tension.

items.title: The lncRNA-encoded micropeptide ANCHOR promotes lateral root growth and drought tolerance in rice
items.summary_raw: Lateral roots (LRs) are important components of plant root systems, determining the robustness of root system architecture and influencing water uptake efficiency. Enhancing the phenotypic plasticity of LRs is key to improving crop production under fluctuating environmental conditions. In this study, we identified ANCHOR, a micropeptide encoded by a long noncoding RNA that is predominantly expressed in LR primordia and plumules. Overexpression of ANCHOR resulted in significantly longer and wider LRs, thereby altering root system architecture and enhancing drought tolerance; knockouts of ANCHOR produced the opposite phenotypes. Mechanistically, ANCHOR localized to plastids and directly interacted with the lysine biosynthetic enzyme LL-diaminopimelate aminotransferase 1 (LL-DAPAT). Our results indicate that ANCHOR functions as a “molecular glue” that enhances DAPAT dimerization. Through its influence on lysine metabolism, ANCHOR raises the levels of the auxin biosynthetic precursor tryptophan, thereby affecting auxin homeostasis. These findings show that lncRNA-derived micropeptides, like their precursor RNAs, can function as fine-tuning regulators. This function of micropeptides, together with their small molecular size, may make them suitable for application as bioeffectors to stimulate root growth and improve plant tolerance to abiotic stress without side effects for plants.

items.title: Dlx1&2 directly promote expression of Cxcl14 to control synapse development and interneuron survival
items.summary_raw: Dlx genes have fundamental roles in the generation, differentiation, and functions of virtually all forebrain GABAergic neurons. Here we used scRNA-Seq to identify genes that are dysregulated in Dlx1/2 conditional mutants in mouse immature CGE- and MGE-derived cortical and olfactory bulb GABAergic interneurons. Dlx1/2 -regulated genes included Cxcl14 and Nr2f2 that are important for cortical interneuron (CIN) survival. We also identified DLX2-bound putative regulatory elements (pREs) of these Dlx -regulated genes. Within the Dlx -expressing lineage, some DLX-bound pREs were specific to CINs, others appeared to be constitutively bound; the latter class having activity in mature CINs. One such pRE and its associated gene, Cxcl14 , is strongly activated by Dlx1/2 and is essential for synaptogenesis onto CINs.

items.title: Ionic liquid–mediated cellular loading for whole tumor cell vaccines
items.summary_raw: Conventional whole tumor cell cancer vaccines have demonstrated limited clinical success due to insufficient immunogenicity and challenges in adjuvant codelivery, despite their rich antigen repertoire and high patient-specific activity. Here, we introduce a simple, single-step approach to load immunostimulatory CpG oligodeoxynucleotides into tumor cells undergoing immunogenic cell death using an ionic liquid–containing cocktail. Results indicate that these adjuvant-loaded tumor cells (referred to as IL-Vax) enhance the uptake of cell-based vaccines by dendritic cells and their subsequent activation, leading to potent antitumor immunity. IL-Vax offered strong protection against tumor growth in a prophylactic B16F10 melanoma mouse model. Furthermore, IL-Vax synergized with PD-1 blockade to slow tumor growth and extend survival in a therapeutic model. The modularity of IL-Vax enables the loading of different cargos or cargo combinations, which may be conducive for additional tailoring of such vaccines and potentially other cell loading applications.

items.title: Rapid green leaf volatile sensing allows intact plants to release induced volatiles earlier than wounded emitters
items.summary_raw: Organisms in the vicinity of attacked neighbors can respond to danger cues by activating their own defenses. However, the temporal dynamics of these interactions remain poorly resolved, despite their importance for the ensuing effects. Here, we investigated defense responses of maize plants that are exposed to induced volatiles from herbivory-induced neighbors in real time. These experiments revealed a surprising temporal paradox: Intact neighbors start emitting most induced volatiles 15 to 80 min earlier than the attacked plants themselves. This earlier responsiveness was not associated with earlier induction of defense hormones, volatile biosynthesis genes, or within-leaf volatile accumulation. Instead, receiver plants kept their stomata open, while attacked sender plants rapidly closed them, likely because of water loss. Using different volatile deficient mutants, we demonstrate that the rapid responses in receivers are triggered by green leaf volatiles, which are released from the wound sites of sender plants within minutes independently of stomatal aperture. Thus, nonattacked neighbors can act as “unhindered observers” that activate some defenses more quickly than attacked organisms themselves, as they do not have to deal with wound trauma. The resulting plant volatile concatenation patterns expand our understanding of volatile signaling and have the potential to shape population-level multitrophic interactions.

items.title: Auxiliary BKβ4 subunits promote nanoscale coupling between BK and voltage-gated calcium channels
items.summary_raw: Intracellular Ca 2+ signals are essential for many cellular processes but must be tightly regulated to ensure precise spatial and temporal control. The large conductance calcium- and voltage-activated K + channel (BK) integrates intracellular Ca 2+ signaling and membrane depolarization to generate hyperpolarizing K + currents that regulate membrane excitability. In many cell types, BK channels achieve rapid activation through functional coupling with voltage-gated calcium (Ca V ) channels that provide localized Ca 2+ signals. However, the mechanisms that regulate the nanoscale organization of BK+Ca V channel complexes remain poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the BK auxiliary subunit β 4 (BKβ 4 ), which is widely expressed throughout the brain and modulates BK gating properties, influences the spatial organization and functional coupling of BK and Ca V channels. Using proximity ligation assays, electrophysiology, and superresolution stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we show that BKβ 4 promotes BK+Ca V nanodomain organization by increasing channel clustering and altering their spatial proximity at the plasma membrane. These structural changes enhance functional coupling between Ca 2+ influx and BK channel activation. Notably, the effects of BKβ 4 on nanodomain organization and coupling depend on the Ca V subtype involved. Together, our findings reveal that the BKβ 4 auxiliary subunit regulates the nanoscale architecture of BK+Ca V channel complexes…

items.title: Extreme weather is creating a perfect storm of misinformation. Here’s what’s at stake.
items.summary_raw: Extreme weather is creating a perfect storm of misinformation a perfect storm of misinformation Rumors and conspiracies are spreading too fast for emergency managers to keep up. This information chaos is slowing disaster relief and putting lives at risk. By Sara Herschander, Vox Nov 1, 2026 This story is part of Distorted , a Grist series exploring the spread of misinformation in the wake of extreme weather. It is published with support from the CO2 Foundation. ​ You likely remember the 2023 Maui wildfires, a tragedy that killed more than 100 people and destroyed nearly 2,000 homes, all but erasing a historic island community. You may also remember that the fires began when a broken power pole owned by the local electric utility sparked against dry vegetation on a windy day. But do you really know that? Were you there? How can you prove it? In the aftermath of the Maui fires, thousands of people across all the major social media platforms shared posts and videos alleging that the fires had a more sinister origin. They posited that the government had used a “direct energy weapon,” or a form of laser, to ignite the area. Depending on the post you saw, this was part of a plot to reclaim the area for a high-speed rail line, or a high-tech “smart city.” A number of right-wing activists and social media personalities amplified these claims, including the late Charlie Kirk. At the same time, the Federal Emergency Management Agency saw accounts linked to China circulating rumors…

items.title: Would you trust an emergency alert written by AI?
items.summary_raw: Earlier this month, after Hurricane Isaias made landfall on the Gulf Coast as a Category 3 hurricane, the emergency management expert Laura Myers got a call from a meteorologist in Alabama. Myers is director of the University of Alabama’s Center for Advanced Public Safety, and she talks to state and local emergency managers around her region all the time. The meteorologist told Myers that a local emergency manager had published a graphic showing where Isaias might threaten the Alabama coast with a “sting jet” of high winds. The problem? The emergency manager had generated the graphic using an artificial intelligence chatbot, and it wasn’t accurate. “That county emergency manager was trying to get his stakeholders to focus on the risk in that county, and so he had asked AI to help him,” she said. “It did what he wanted it to do, but it was not meteorologically accurate.” Most emergency management agencies don’t permit employees to use generative AI, but Myers and most other emergency management experts agree that its usage is likely already pervasive at state and local disaster departments. There are hundreds of companies that are marketing AI tools to emergency managers for tasks like flood damage assessment and resource coordination, but public communication is one of the areas where government employees and startups have the most interest. The reason? Most emergency managers aren’t very good at sending out alerts and quickly communicating about disasters with the public…

items.title: How to fact-check during and after a disaster
items.summary_raw: Misinformation about extreme weather and disasters often starts small: Someone reposts a rumor on social media about government corruption or an AI photo of a shark swimming in floodwaters. It’s shared dozens, then hundreds, then thousands of times before huge swaths of people believe it as truth. Trying to fact-check during a crisis is stressful, and extreme weather makes you feel like there’s a lot to figure out and learn in a short period of time. That’s why it’s important to know ahead of time who you can trust, how to vet information, and how to talk to your friends and family about it. Extreme weather is creating a perfect storm of misinformation Would you trust an emergency alert written by AI? Why trust Grist? Where to find accurate information about extreme weather Many well-intentioned people want to do their own research. But not all sources of information are equal — especially when your safety is on the line. Finding the right sources will help you avoid falling for — or fueling — rumors that aren’t true. Below is a list of reliable sources for extreme weather alerts, updates, and more. Your local emergency agency: Your city, county, and state has an emergency management department. Emergency managers handle response efforts and communicate with the public in their jurisdiction about the disaster. items.title: Climate security narratives in transboundary river basins: the discursive politics of the Helmand River Basin
items.summary_raw: Climate security has moved from a marginal environmental concern to a central issue in politics, particularly in transboundary river basins. This study examines how competing climate security narratives are constructed and mobilised in hydropolitical interactions in the transboundary Helmand River Basin. Rather than simply reflecting hydrological or climatic realities, these narratives reveal discursive struggles over responsibility, policy priorities, and governance. Building on critical securitisation scholarship, the paper adapts and extends a framework of climate security discourse to the Helmand context. Based on a qualitative, interpretive analysis of official statements, media reports, and diplomatic documents, it shows that Afghan actors describe drought and climate variability as existential threats, while Iranian discourse emphasises governance failures, treaty obligations, and upstream hydraulic missions. These competing narratives shape hydropolitical interactions, water policies, and prospects for cooperation. The findings suggest that reframing climate security debates around accountability, transparency, and shared governance can foster trust and support cooperation.

items.title: Societal readiness for just energy transitions: toward an integrated conceptual framework
items.summary_raw: The success of energy transitions depends not only on technological innovation and policy interventions but also on societies' ability to understand, support, participate in, and adapt to transition-related change. Although societal readiness has received growing attention in sustainability, innovation, and responsible research and innovation research, it remains insufficiently integrated into the just energy transition literature. Existing studies rarely treat societal readiness as a distinct construct, instead addressing related concepts such as social acceptance, trust, participation, justice, governance capacity, institutional preparedness, and adaptive capacity in isolation. This fragmentation limits understanding of the conditions that enable equitable and effective transitions. This mini-review synthesizes literature that explicitly or implicitly addresses societal readiness in just energy transitions and develops an integrated conceptual framework. The review identifies four interconnected dimensions: social acceptance and trust; participation and justice; governance and institutional capacity; and socio-economic and adaptive capacity. Together, these dimensions capture the conditions that shape the ability of individuals, communities, and governance systems to engage with and support transition processes. Research has focused primarily on social acceptance, participation, and justice, while behavioral and discursive indicators, multidimensional assessment…

items.title: Exploring the Determinants of Green Purchase Intention and Behavior Among College Students in Fujian Province, China
items.summary_raw: Purpose: This study aims to identify the key determinants of green purchase intention and green purchase behavior among college students in Fujian, China. The study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior by incorporating environmental concern and environmental knowledge to provide a broader explanation of green purchasing decisions. Research design, data and methodology: A quantitative research approach was applied using structured questionnaires administered to 500 students from the Department of Business Administration at Meizhouwan Vocational Technology College in Fujian, China. All respondents had prior experience purchasing green products. A non-probability sampling approach combining purposive, quota, and convenience sampling was adopted. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling to evaluate the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. Results: Environmental concern, environmental knowledge, attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control all had significant positive effects on green purchase intention. Environmental concern showed the strongest effect, followed by perceived behavioral control and environmental knowledge. Attitude and subjective norms also had significant effects. Green purchase intention significantly influenced green purchase behavior. Conclusions: The findings support the applicability of the extended TPB framework in explaining green purchasing behavior among college students and…

What makes community energy solutions last? Shared internet as a governance anchor for microgrid longevity in the Amazon – A mixed-methods study
items.summary_raw: Solar microgrids are a promising solution for remote electrification, yet many face sustainability challenges tied to governance, maintenance, and collective action. This paper argues that shared digital connectivity plays a critical, yet underexplored, role in reshaping electricity's social value off-grid. Using mixed-methods evidence from two community-managed solar microgrids in the Brazilian Amazon, we examine how internet connectivity reconfigures incentives for collective action and long-term stewardship. Our findings show that when electricity enables digital connectivity, energy infrastructures shift from low-priority goods to high-value systems, strengthening local governance, financial contributions, and maintenance engagement. Conceptualizing connectivity as a socio-institutional anchor, this study contributes to energy social science debates on governance and sustainability, offering a replicable framework for the Global South to overcome the ‘build-and-abandon’ cycle in off-grid projects.

items.title: Communicating Climate-Related Risks via Storytelling and Statistics
items.summary_raw: Strategies are needed to effectively communicate the public health effects associated with climate change-amplified events, e.g., floods, wildfires, and heat waves. This review explores ways to translate complex statistics and present other critical aspects of climate change using storytelling (through narratives, exemplars, and images) to engage people and maximize comprehension and healthy behaviors. We also examine how to shape the strategy or strategies used based on audience characteristics such as adult age, numeracy, literacy, and ideology. We delineate the key psychological levers through which these strategies work-effort reduction, emotions, psychological distance, efficacy, and presence of relevant numbers-and propose a barrier-matched framework to choose communication approaches. We also illustrate key concepts with case studies. Developing long-term capacity to deliver effective messages is one step toward empowering people to act safely in response to threats, build a more resilient society, enhance quality of life, and save money and lives.

items.title: Unveiling Trends in Natural Language Processing Research for Public Policy: A Bibliometric Analysis and Dynamic Topic Modeling Approach
items.source_name: Journal of Information Systems Engineering and Business Intelligence
items.summary_raw: Background: Natural Language Processing (NLP), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI), has advanced rapidly and can now analyze large volumes of textual data to extract meaningful information. This is highly relevant for supporting evidence-based, responsive, and accountable public policy through efficient analysis of public opinion, policy documents, and academic literature. Objective: This study maps research trends in the application of NLP to public policy through a bibliometric analysis and Dynamic Topic Modeling (DTM) approach, identifying the current topic structure, the temporal evolution of research themes, and the topics that may inform future research agendas. Methods: Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, publications from 2016–2025 were retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases and screened through a multi-stage selection process. A total of 1,134 publications were included in the final bibliometric analysis. The resulting abstracts were analyzed using BERTopic-based DTM. The best-performing hyperparameter configuration, chosen after comparing several candidates, achieved coherence and topic diversity scores, as well as an outlier ratio, within generally acceptable ranges, yielding a set of primary topics plus a smaller outlier topic. Results: Publications grew from fewer than 70 per year before 2021 to 377 in 2025, led by China (317), the United States (181), and India (158). items.title: Reducing car use to support local climate goals: The potential role of small and medium-sized employers
items.source_name: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
items.summary_raw: Widespread adoption of Transport Demand Management (TDM) would significantly reduce congestion, pollution, and carbon emissions. Employers can implement some TDM measures more quickly and acceptably than measures which must be implemented by authorities. This study evaluates the role of employers in achieving TDM targets, including small and medium employers (SMEs). The role of SMEs in implementing TDM strategies has been under-researched despite them comprising most private-sector employment. We evaluated demand for employer-led TDM measures using a Travel to Work survey from the West of England (n=20,017). Employees commuting by car reported which measures would facilitate walking, cycling, public transport, car-sharing to work, and purchasing a battery electric vehicle (BEV). We categorised these ‘enablers’ based on whether they could be implemented by employers (e.g., lockers) or required government action (e.g., cycle lanes). Results suggest authority-led measures, like improved infrastructure and public transport provision, are the primary enablers of modal shift. However, employers can meaningfully support shifts to walking, cycling, car sharing, and purchasing a BEV. Employers should prioritise the adoption of showering facilities, drying rooms, storage lockers and secure cycle parking to achieve modal shift. SMEs could enable an equal, if not greater, proportion of their employees to cycle as their larger counterparts. Results invite a re-assessment of the impact of…
