items.title: Contrasting Roles of Geothermal Energy and Fossil Fuels in Indonesia's Carbon Emissions
items.summary_raw: The transition toward renewable energy is essential for improving environmental quality and mitigating climate change, particularly in fossil fuel-dependent emerging economies. Indonesia has substantial geothermal energy potential, yet its energy mix remains heavily reliant on fossil fuels, highlighting the importance of assessing geothermal energy's contribution to carbon emission reduction. This study investigates the dynamic impacts of geothermal energy in comparison with coal, oil, and gas on environmental quality in Indonesia, proxied by CO2 emissions from 1990Q1 to 2024Q4. The analysis employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) and Bootstrap Quantile Regression (BQR). The ARDL long-run results indicate that geothermal energy significantly reduces CO2 emissions in the long run. In contrast, coal and oil consumption significantly increase CO2 emissions, while gas shows no significant long-run effect. Among the control variables, FDI and manufacturing value added contribute to CO2 emission reductions in the long run. The BQR results further reveal pronounced heterogeneity, showing that the adverse effects of coal consumption are more pronounced at higher emission quantiles, while oil consumption increases CO2 emissions across all quantiles. Meanwhile, the emission-reducing effect of geothermal energy becomes more evident at higher quantiles of the CO2 emissions distribution. Overall, the results underscore the importance of expanding geothermal energy deployment…

items.title: On combining climate models into weighted ensembles
items.summary_raw: Abstract. Several methods have been proposed and used to refine estimates of future climate change based on combined output from comprehensive climate models. While previously the so-called model democracy approach was used to combine model predictions, where every model is given equal weight, it is now widely accepted that using model weights that account for model performance and model independence is necessary to obtain more reliable results. However, most existing approaches rely, implicitly or explicitly, on a similar statistical basis, while describing things in different ways. Here we distinguish between approaches that are based on the performance of individual models (individual performance weighting) and approaches that are based on the performance of the weighted ensemble as a whole (ensemble performance weighting). At the same time, we formulate both in probabilistic Bayesian terms to make their application and comparison straightforward. Using simple constructed examples, we demonstrate that the ensemble performance weighting approach implicitly accounts for co-dependencies among models, which arguably makes the computation of independence weights for the purpose of model weighting obsolete. We also show that a set of weighted models within the ensemble weighting approach will naturally tend to artificially reduce uncertainty and that this is strongly influenced by the choice of the prior distribution over weight vectors. The distinction between individual and…

items.title: Adaptive Capacity and Climate Change Resilience of Coconut Farmers: A Philippines Case Study
items.summary_raw: Purpose: This qualitative study aims to examine the impacts of climate change on the livelihoods and production systems of coconut farmers, to analyze adaptation practices and strategies through the lens of sustainability and the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework, and to assess farmers’ levels of resilience and adaptive capacity to climate change within the context of the Philippines. Research design, data and methodology: The study employs a qualitative research design, with data collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 43 purposively selected coconut farmers. The data were analyzed using content analysis and thematic synthesis in order to capture farmers’ lived experiences, perceptions, and grassroots-level adaptation practices. Results: The findings indicate that the majority of farmers clearly perceive changes in climatic conditions, particularly increased variability in rainfall, drought, and the frequency of extreme weather events. These changes have had direct impacts on coconut yields, income stability, and household economic security. In terms of adaptation, farmers have adopted a range of sustainable agricultural practices, including efficient water management, the use of organic fertilizers and soil amendments to restore soil quality, and crop diversification to spread production and income risks. These practices contribute to enhancing the resilience of farming systems and demonstrate alignment with the environmental and…

items.title: Informational cues and willingness-to-pay for driverless cars
items.summary_raw: This study examines the influence of social factors on willingness-to-pay (WTP) for autonomous vehicles (AVs), framing social influence through informational cues received from mass media, social media, market penetration, and word-of-mouth (WOM) from social contacts. The impact of WOM is moderated based on the trust level associated with social contacts. We proposed a behavioural framework that links informational cues to AV consideration, and models AV selection as a function of that consideration. Model parameters are estimated using data from a representative sample of 862 Sydney residents, and a latent class approach is used to capture taste heterogeneity. Thanks to the structure of the proposed framework, WTP for automation is estimated conditional on the status of informational cues. The framework offers novel insights into the dynamics of innovation diffusion and the timing of policy interventions. When informational cues are weak and market uptake remains limited, external support may be particularly relevant during the early stages of diffusion. As market uptake increases and the technology generates stronger confirmatory signals through trusted networks, the need for policy support may gradually diminish as diffusion becomes increasingly supported by market experience and social reinforcement.

items.title: Innovation amidst Turmoil, Part 2: Narratives and Sensemaking among German Managers during the Pandemic
items.summary_raw: How actors make sense of complex and uncertain situations shapes their perceived agency to foster innovation and organizational change. We present a case study on the sensemaking processes of German managers during the COVID-19 pandemic to gain insights for researchers and decision-makers interested in navigating uncertainty. Based on data collected (n=209) via an online questionnaire and grounded in theories of sensemaking and narrative discourse analysis, we identify seven distinct narratives that reveal varying perceptions of agency, problem framing, and modes of acting under uncertainty: “Business as usual”, “early mover”, “stronger together”, “step-by-step”, “bold leadership”, “acting impossible”, and “against the tide”. Based on our case study, we identify promising avenues for future research and discuss the practical relevance of proactive and collective sensemaking, emotions, detecting weak signals, and future-oriented narratives in economics for decision-making under uncertainty as well as perceptions of agency in (organizational) innovation. JEL Codes: D80, D91, H12, I19, L21, M14, O31, O35, Z13

items.title: Disaster Narratives and Forestry Policy: A Comparative Analysis of National and Regional Media Coverage of the 2025 Sumatra Floods
items.source_name: KASTA Jurnal Ilmu Sosial Agama Budaya dan Terapan
items.summary_raw: The 2025 Sumatra floods generated policy debate across Southeast Asia. Media coverage demonstrates how news organizations frame crises and legitimize particular policy responses in their role as policy actors. This study compares the elements and strategies of media policy narratives in Indonesia, Singapore, and Malaysia using the meso-level Narrative Policy Framework (NPF). It applies qualitative content analysis to 309 online news articles published between November 2025 and May 2026. The findings show that Indonesian media exhibit the strongest combination of containment (90.5%) and angel-shift (85.3%), constructing a Story of Control that positions the government as the Hero and privileges domestic solutions. Singaporean media maintain a high level of angel-shift (92.3%) in operational elements while increasing expansion (20.5%) in structural elements, shifting the narrative toward a Story of Decline and demands for accountability. Malaysian media display the highest levels of expansion (25.4%) and devil-shift (22.0%), casting corporations as Villains and constructing Stymied Progress narratives oriented toward regional reform. These three patterns correspond to each country's National Narrative Position, defined by the interaction of media ownership linkages with state actors, press freedom scores, and the media's structural position relative to the event, rather than by actors' belief coalitions as assumed in conventional NPF applications. The findings support three…

items.title: Pushing for more: Policy norms and climate clubs in global politics
items.summary_raw: Normative clubs have emerged as a prominent governance tool in global politics. Such clubs are a voluntary, minilateral form of international cooperation whereby members make a normative commitment to certain policy objectives. Particularly within climate and energy governance, normative clubs seek to influence state behaviour not primarily through material incentives or sanctions, but through shared norms and expectations of appropriate conduct. But scholarship on clubs has generally ignored International Relations theory and research on norms. This paper develops a typology of norms mobilized by such clubs to examine how different norm types forge, stabilize, and diffuse behavioural expectations in global climate politics and governance. We distinguish three types of policy norms: (1) appropriateness - conferring norms , which define what it means to be a responsible and legitimate actor; (2) prohibitive norms , which delineate practices that are no longer acceptable; and (3) aspirational norms , which articulate forward-looking goals toward which members are encouraged to work. Using illustrative case studies of the Coalition of Finance Ministers for Climate Action, the Powering Past Coal Alliance, and the Climate Neutrality Coalition, the paper shows how these norm types operate in practice. The analysis highlights how normative clubs combine soft obligations, persuasion, and benchmarking to influence policy debates and international expectations, even in the absence of…

items.title: Perceptions, Knowledge, and Adaptive actions in Response to Climate Events: A Scoping Review of Climate Health Literacy among Community Dwelling Older Adults
items.summary_raw: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Extreme climate events can threaten older adults' health. The purpose of this study was to summarize existing literature on older adults' climate health literacy, defined as their ability to find and access, understand, and act upon information related to climate-related health threats. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in the bibliographic databases Embase, Medline and Scopus and grey literature sources Cornell Initiative for Research on Climate and Aging and Climate Change and Human Health Literature portals with searches updated January 2026. English language studies of community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and older were included if they reported at least one aspect of climate health literacy. Quantitative data were reported as median percentages, and qualitative themes were categorized. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies, including 22,992 records for 20,296 unique participants, were included. Most recognized the health risks of extreme climate events but did not identify personal vulnerability. Television was the most cited source of information and hydration, clothing and environment modification, and activity adjustment were the most utilized adaptive actions. Barriers to adaptive actions included financial constraints, limited mobility and lack of supports. The effectiveness of studied interventions was mixed, influenced by intervention type and study design. DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Despite access to information…

items.title: SHEAR PERFORMANCE OF NAIL-FASTENED SHEATHING-TO-FRAMING CONNECTIONS IN CEMENT-BAMBOO FRAME SYSTEMS
items.summary_raw: The increasing demand for sustainable and affordable housing has encouraged the development of engineered bamboo construction systems such as Cement-Bamboo Frame Technology (CBFT), which integrates bamboo framing with cement-based cladding. Although previous studies have demonstrated the structural performance of CBFT and bamboo shear wall systems, limited research has investigated the localized behavior of nail-fastened sheathing-to-framing connections. This study experimentally evaluated the monotonic shear behavior of CBFT nail-fastened connections at the subassembly level. Eight connection configurations with rib lath and flattened bamboo cladding were tested with five replicates each by varying cladding type, stud orientation, nail quantity, and mortar infill. Load–displacement responses were analyzed to determine yield load, ultimate load, initial stiffness, ductility, and energy absorption, while failure modes and statistical significance were evaluated. Results showed that mortar infill and increased nail quantity significantly improved connection performance. The rib lath configuration with three staggered nails and mortar infill achieved the highest initial stiffness (839.87 N/mm), yield load (1418.38 N), and ultimate load (1726.64 N), whereas the flattened bamboo configuration with three nails and mortar infill achieved the highest energy absorption (50,272.26 N·mm). Mortar confinement shifted failure from nail pull-out to nail bending and cladding damage…

items.title: Fusion confusion: What makes fusion energy hard to grasp and how communicators might respond
items.summary_raw: Fusion energy is widely discussed as a promising long-term solution to global energy and climate challenges, yet public understanding of the technology remains limited. While much of the science and energy communication literature focuses on comprehension barriers among lay and non-expert audiences, empirical studies examining communication and comprehension barriers in fusion science remain scarce, particularly in the United States. Drawing on research identifying jargon and technical complexity as key barriers to understanding, this study investigates whether non-expert audiences struggle to understand fusion-related information, why, how they interpret key fusion concepts and jargon, and which communication strategies support clearer understanding and greater trust. We conducted an online survey of U.S. adults, complemented by semi-structured interviews with a highly educated sample. Results show widespread awareness of fusion energy but persistent uncertainty about its safety and feasibility. Participants frequently struggled with technical ideas, jargon, and comprehension, with these difficulties associated with gender, science-related employment, and education level. Comprehension barriers were evident even among highly educated respondents, suggesting that difficulties arise not only from limited public knowledge but also from how fusion science is communicated. The results indicate that effective communication strategies must address jargon and technical complexity…

items.title: Recalled vs. Experienced Emotions as Drivers of Pro-Environmental Behaviour: Experimental Evidence from Ghana and the Philippines
items.summary_raw: Emotions are widely invoked to motivate climate action, yet how different forms of emotional activation translate into costly, real-world pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) remains unclear. This study examines whether positive emotions triggered by (i) recalling past PEB and (ii) engaging with environmental social media content increase subsequent donations to an environmental NGO. We implemented incentivised 2×2 between-subjects experiments among middle-class respondents in Ghana (N = 789) and the Philippines (N = 972) between April and May 2022, comparing the individual and combined effects of these two interventions on real donation decisions, and testing the mediating role of self-reported positive emotion. In the Philippines, both recall and engagement significantly increased donation amounts, with recall showing a robust effect across model specifications and indicative evidence of a small, partial mediation via positive emotions. The combined treatment, however, did not yield an interaction effect, suggesting additive rather than synergistic impacts. In Ghana, neither intervention nor emotional responses predicted donations; instead, beliefs about donation effectiveness and sociodemographic characteristics were the main predictors of environmental donations. These cross-country differences suggest that emotional drivers of climate engagement may be culturally and contextually contingent rather than universal. By experimentally contrasting recalled and experienced…

items.title: The Juliana v. United States case and the Global Youth Climate Movement: An Aristotelian Rhetorical Analysis of Climate Change Communication
items.source_name: Principia an international journal of epistemology
items.summary_raw: Despite the overwhelming scientific consensus on anthropogenic climate change, public skepticism and motivational deficits persist. Effective climate change communication requires not only presenting scientific information but also conveying the real, ongoing impacts of climate disruption. This paper examines Juliana v. United States, a landmark youth-led climate lawsuit, through the lens of Aristotelian rhetoric to demonstrate how emotional appeals (pathos) enhance the effectiveness of climate change communication. The study analyzes how climate litigation cases function not only as a legal tool but also as a powerful communicative resource capable of shaping public understanding and mobilizing civic engagement. The analysis highlights how the Plaintiffs’ narratives in the Juliana case — detailing personal, emotional, cultural, and spiritual harms —translate abstract scientific risks into concrete lived experiences. Emotions such as fear, indignation, and pity alter the hearers’ state, both public and judicial, and influence their judgments. Situated within Aristotle’s framework of logos, ethos, and pathos, the case exemplifies how pathos can ethically support deliberation, address epistemic inequalities, and persuade audiences of the gravity of climate change. Although the lawsuit ultimately failed to reach trial, it catalyzed global youth-led climate litigation and contributed significantly to public discourse by framing climate change as an already unfolding crisis. The…

items.title: Beyond the environmental burden narrative: environmental attitudes and green-job aspirations among Syrian refugees and Jordanians
items.summary_raw: Abstract There is a prevalent view of refugees as an environmental burden, a narrative that can exacerbate strained relations between refugees and host communities. This study examines the empirical basis of this perspective using an original, in-person survey of 510 Syrian refugees and 509 Jordanian nationals across four cities in Jordan: Amman, Mafraq, Irbid, and Zarqa. The findings indicate that environmental attitudes and practices are broadly similar among Jordanians and Syrian refugees. Syrian refugees report modestly higher levels of environmental knowledge, a pattern that may reflect exposure to climate-related risks during war and displacement. In addition, Syrian refugees express greater interest in green jobs than Jordanians do, a pattern that may be associated with their disadvantaged position in the labor market and their search for new employment opportunities. These findings suggest that, under the right institutional design, refugees can contribute to the host nation’s green economy transition.

items.title: Early Climate Impact Assessments Targeted 2025—How Did They Perform for Global Water Resources?
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Climate impact studies from the 1990s produced projections for global water resources extending to 2025. We evaluate the first two global water resource assessments and the IPCC's 2001 statements on future water resources against subsequent observations. Temperature projections were broadly consistent with what has since been observed. The studies projected a small increase in global precipitation, with increases at high latitudes and decreases in the subtropics; this pattern is consistent with present‐day model projections, though robust observed changes have yet to emerge. Runoff projections for 2025 are hard to assess given limited data and multi‐year variability, but warming effects on snowmelt‐dominated streamflow are consistent with observations. Population projections matched (8.23 billion observed versus 8.01–8.06 billion projected), whereas water demand projections overestimated the increase in water withdrawals (+13% observed versus +19%–52% projected). The IPCC's 2001 projections of impacts on water resources were consistent with its 2021/2022 assessment. These early studies proved influential in research and policy, initiating a proliferation of global water modeling and climate impact assessments. We discuss how the scope of such assessments has evolved. Despite improvements, challenges remain, including uncertainty in runoff and water use data, alongside scope for better water stress indicators and use of earth observation. items.title: INTENTION TO ADOPT CLIMATE-RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AMONG WHEAT FARMERS IN PUNJAB, PAKISTAN: AN EXTENDED THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOUR
items.summary_raw: This study aimed to investigate the psychosocial determinants of wheat growers' intention to adopt a specific set of climate-resilient agricultural practices (CRAPs) in the Punjab Province of Pakistan, which is an extended Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) including attitude, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, trust in CRAPs performance, and current climate-resilient practice management (past behaviour). In May–July 2024, a cross-sectional survey of 384 wheat growers was carried out involving a six-stage design, purposively sampled agro-ecological zones, districts, tehsils, and randomly sampled union councils, villages, and growers. The five CRAPs were conservation tillage, certified heat- and drought-tolerant varieties, timely sowing, stage-based balanced fertilisation and critical-stage irrigation. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used for data analysis with 10,000 subsamples generated by bootstrapping. Attitude was the strongest positive predictor of intention (β = 0.446; 95% CI 0.319–0.543; p < 0.001), followed by trust in CRAPs performance (β = 0.344; p < 0.001) and perceived behavioural control (β = 0.172; p = 0.001). Subjective norms were not significant (β = 0.038; p = 0.455). Despite a positive bivariate correlation with intention, current CRAP management had a negative partial coefficient (β = −0.246; p < 0.001). This is a pattern of statistical suppression or a “ceiling effect,” not a pattern of resistance to change…

items.title: Top-down public engagement on climate action: Ireland’s National Dialogue on Climate Action
items.summary_raw: The ‘democratic wave’ in relation to citizen involvement in climate change policy challenges is illustrated here in the Irish context through the Citizens’ Assembly on Climate Change. The National Dialogue on Climate Action (NDCA) has sought to broaden the time and space for citizen input into climate change policy formation. The NDCA positions Ireland as continuing to innovate within democratic processes. This note reflects upon the NDCA for the years 2021–2025. We first outline the national policy context in which these deliberative mechanisms emerged, situating Ireland’s decarbonisation pathway in relation to European emissions ceilings. Following this, we provide a historical and contextual brief on citizen engagement in Irish climate policy which laid the foundations for the establishment of the NDCA. We outline the conceptual foundations of the NDCA before outlining its four main pillars. Finally, we reflect upon the impact of such processes and outline ways forward for national policy mechanisms to co-create decarbonisation pathways with citizens. This note serves to position the NDCA temporally, in relation to national engagement on climate change, and internationally in relation to policy innovations for citizen involvement in climate change policy.

items.title: Pro‐environmental claims versus carbon realities: Behavioural insights of smallholder mandarin farmers in Nepal
items.summary_raw: Abstract Agriculture is one of the major sources of greenhouse gas emissions, and promoting Pro‐Environmental Behaviour (PEB) among farmers offers substantial potential for climate change mitigation. However, understanding of the psychological factors shaping farmers' perceived PEB and how these perceptions align with their actual environmental performance remains limited. This study applied Ajzen's Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and employed covariance‐based structural equation modelling to explore relationships among attitude, subjective norms, Perceived Behavioural Control (PBC), behavioural intention and PEB, alongside a comparison between self‐reported and actual PEB. A web‐based Qualtrics survey was conducted to assess perceived PEB, and semi‐structured interviews were used to collect farm‐level data to estimate carbon footprint as a proxy for actual behaviour among 120 mandarin farmers in Syangja, Nepal, selected using a multi‐stage sampling approach. Attitude and PBC were strong predictors of behavioural intention, while subjective norms showed weaker influence. Behavioural intention significantly predicted PEB and education, training participation and household income moderated several of these relationships, highlighting socio‐economic variation in behavioural determinants. Comparison between perceived and actual PEB revealed a moderate correlation, with 71% of the variance unexplained. This indicates a substantial gap between farmers' self‐perceptions and their…

items.title: Closing the climate–economics communication gap
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02784-w As the IPCC is in its seventh assessment cycle, bridging the gap between physical climate science and economics has become more urgent. Estimating climate damages requires a rigorous translation of physical hazards into economic losses, highlighting the need for better communication between the disciplines.

items.title: Feedstock quality gradients and net energy constraints in sustainable aviation fuel: a biophysical economic assessment of the HEFA pathway
items.summary_raw: Despite extensive policy support and climate commitments, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) remains more expensive than conventional jet fuel. Hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids (HEFA) are currently the dominant commercial SAF pathway. This paper evaluates a narrower proposition: whether differences in lipid-feedstock quality create a biophysical mechanism that could contribute to persistent production-cost differences as HEFA deployment expands. The analysis is structural and comparative rather than a time-series or causal model of observed prices. Using a biophysical-economics framework, this study compares the external energy required to acquire, prepare, and convert used cooking oil (UCO), conventional crop oils, and purpose-grown oil crops. Under midpoint assumptions for external input and liquid-energy recovery, external-energy EROI is approximately 4.06:1 for UCO, 1.55:1 for conventional crop oils, and 1.82:1 for purpose-grown oil crops. The corresponding full-combination envelopes are 3.0–5.9, 0.99–3.2, and 1.3–3.2, respectively; these envelopes combine favorable or unfavorable parameter endpoints and are not probability distributions. The UCO baseline applies a cut-off attribution convention: no original agricultural-production burden is assigned after the oil has completed its first use, although collection, transport, pretreatment, hydrogen, and conversion energy are included. This convention is not a claim that UCO is physically burden-free. Reassigning 25%…

items.title: Influence of Geopolitical Risk on Energy Transition and Climate Change
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Geopolitical tensions can influence energy transition, which, in turn, can impact climate change. Thus, we construct a framework that integrates these processes, analyzing 17 economies from 1990 to 2020 using a GVAR model. We hypothesize that geopolitical risk shocks affect economies through domestic financial markets. The results demonstrate that geopolitical risk shocks (i) hinder national energy transitions and contribute to increased carbon emissions; (ii) induce fluctuations in financial markets; (iii) have a minor direct impact on energy transition, except in Scandinavia and the United States; (iv) indirectly influence economies through financial markets (particularly stock markets); and (v) generate spillover effects and heterogeneities. We corroborate our findings through shock identification, treating financial markets as conduits for the geopolitical risk shock. Additionally, we conduct a battery of robustness checks addressing structural breaks, time‐varying bilateral trade, and bilateral financial flows (instead of bilateral trade), all of which confirm the consistency of our results. We conclude by discussing fiscal policies aimed at counterbalancing the negative effects of geopolitical risk on energy transition and climate change, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation for the effectiveness of these policies.

items.title: Integration of third-generation concentrated solar power and solid oxide electrolysis for dispatchable solar hydrogen production: Multi-variable optimization and techno-economic assessment
items.summary_raw: This study presents a third-generation (Gen3) concentrated solar power (CSP) system integrated with solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) for dispatchable hydrogen production. The configuration combines a liquid sodium central receiver, ternary chloride molten salt (MgCl 2 -KCl-NaCl) thermal energy storage, a recompression supercritical CO 2 Brayton cycle operating at 700°C, and an SOEC at 800°C. System performance is evaluated using an integrated thermodynamic, exergy, exergoeconomic, and techno-economic framework under Almería, Spain conditions (direct normal irradiance, DNI, 2240 kWh/m 2 /yr). The baseline system achieves a 69.5% capacity factor, substantially exceeding typical second-generation CSP plants, with overall energy and exergy efficiencies of 24.2% and 25.7%, respectively. Component-level exergoeconomic analysis identifies the SOEC stack and receiver assembly as dominant cost drivers, confirming that capital cost reduction is the primary improvement pathway. Multi-variable genetic algorithm optimization identifies a global optimum achieving a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH 2 ) of 3.84 $/kg at a 70.9% capacity factor. Techno-economic assessment shows that electricity cost is the dominant economic driver: reducing it from 55.66 to 20 $/MWh lowers LCOH 2 by approximately 1.19 $/kg, more than three times the benefit achievable through complete SOEC maturation by 2050. items.title: Synchronous end-Permian mass extinction zenith in marine and low–middle latitude terrestrial North China
items.summary_raw: The end-Permian mass extinction was the most severe biotic crisis of the Phanerozoic, yet temporal synchrony between marine and terrestrial extinctions remains debated due to correlation uncertainties. Here, we present an integrated magnetostratigraphic, cyclostratigraphic, and carbon-isotope and mercury (Hg) chemostratigraphic record from the fluvial Upper Shihhotse, Sunjiagou, and Liujiagou formations at the Sigou section, North China. We identify 14 magnetozones spanning the late Changhsingian to late Olenekian, constrained by a floating timescale based on gamma-ray cyclostratigraphy and subsequently anchored through magnetostratigraphic correlation. Our chronostratigraphy reveals a Hg peak at 252.4 Ma, aligning with the main eruptive phase of the Siberian Traps Large Igneous Province, while the carbon isotope excursion onset (252.1 Ma) and minimum (252.0 Ma) are synchronous with the Meishan Global Stratotype Section and Point. Furthermore, the Induan–Olenekian boundary is positioned below magnetozone SG4n, constraining the Induan Stage duration to 1.6 to 1.8 My. These findings establish a high-resolution chronostratigraphic framework for the Permian–Triassic boundary in North China, supporting a synchronous extinction zenith across marine and low–middle latitude terrestrial ecosystems, with latitudinal diachroneity relative to high-latitude and tropical landmasses.

items.title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes
items.summary_raw: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body’s glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.

items.title: Capture and reduction of singlet oxygen via an anthracene-based framework for stable Li-O 2 batteries
items.summary_raw: Given the increasing global energy demand and rapid advancement of low-carbon technologies, Li-O 2 batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, offering great promise for advanced energy systems. However, the formation of harmful singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) in both discharge and charge processes induces parasitic reactions that deteriorate round-trip efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, an anthracene-based covalent-organic framework (AntCOF) is introduced as a highly effective catalyst for the 1 O 2 reduction reaction (SORR) in Li-O 2 batteries. The conjugated porous framework selectively captures electrophilic 1 O 2 , enabling effective charge transfer from AntCOF to the empty π* orbital of 1 O 2 and promoting SORR in subsequent discharge processes. This mechanism suppresses 1 O 2 diffusion and mitigates associated side reactions, leading to reduced overpotentials and improved cycling performance when coupled with a RuO 2 catalyst. This work may enlighten further investigations into 1 O 2 -related chemistry across a broad range of oxygen-redox electrochemical systems.

items.title: Ectopic expression of melanopsin promotes axonal regeneration in retinal ganglion cells via cAMP and TRPC signaling
items.summary_raw: In mammals, retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) show very minor axonal regeneration following axotomy. Despite genetic and pharmacological efforts to promote this regeneration, progress remains slow and limited, especially in overcoming potentially cell-type-specific barriers. In this paper, we virally expressed melanopsin (OPN4), which is the native photopigment in intrinsically-photosensitive RGCs (ipRGCs), broadly in RGCs. IpRGCs are known to show relative resistance to degeneration and axonal loss after injury. We correlated the exogenous-melanopsin-mediated intrinsic light responses of the successfully infected RGCs (referred to as +OPN4 RGCs) with their ability to show axonal regeneration after an optic-nerve crush. Specifically, we found +OPN4 RGCs to show functional rhabdomeric and ciliary motifs of phototransduction as we previously found in ipRGCs. +OPN4 αRGCs (the largest RGCs in the retina) exhibited light-triggered fast (via TRPC signaling) and slow (via cAMP signaling) response components, whereas +OPN4 non-αRGC responses comprised predominantly just a fast component. Genetic ablation of TRPC channels (TRPC6/7) or group II adenylyl cyclase (AC2/4/7) to abolish the fast or the slow response component, respectively, largely attenuated the axonal regeneration of +OPN4 αRGCs in the optic-nerve-crush model. At the same time, administration of cell-permeant cAMP not only rescued the AC2/4/7-knock-out phenotype in +OPN4 αRGCs but also potentiated axonal regeneration in some…

items.title: Recognition-dependent activation of the Arabidopsis RRS1-R/RPS4 TIR-NLR immune receptor pair
items.summary_raw: Plant TIR domain-containing proteins exhibit NADase activity upon pathogen effector recognition, creating small molecules that activate defense via EDS1 and its associated proteins. Arabidopsis RPS4 and RRS1 comprise a TIR-NLR immune receptor pair that recognizes multiple effector proteins including AvrRps4 and PopP2. We show here that RPS4 and RRS1 acquire NADase activity upon recognition of a cognate effector. However, both in the presence and absence of effector, RPS4 and RRS1 form an oligomer that does not change in size upon effector provision. Effector-dependent defense activation by RPS4 and RRS1 requires the catalytic glutamate residue and the BB-loop motif of RPS4, which is absent in RRS1 and other RRS1-like TIR domains in Arabidopsis . Oligomerization of RPS4 and RRS1 occurs through multiple domains, but oligomerization does not require enzymatic activity. We propose that conformational changes or reconfiguration within the RPS4/RRS1 oligomer upon effector recognition derepresses the complex for immune activation.

items.title: Septin binding restricts Shigella growth and triggers intracellular tolerance
items.summary_raw: Pathogen survival relies on their ability to adapt to changing environments, yet how intracellular bacteria tolerate cell-autonomous immunity remains unclear. Septins assemble into cage-like structures around cytoplasmic Shigella targeted by autophagy, but their antibacterial activity was unknown. Using advanced microscopy and cell-free reconstitution, we show that septins polymerize into circumferentially oriented filaments that inhibit bacterial growth. RNA-sequencing reveals that septin binding to Shigella upregulates type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors and triggers a stress response. Underlying this, septin-bound Shigella possess hyperpolarized membranes, but without lethally damaged cell envelope. We show that exposure to septin binding enhances the impact of the cell envelope-targeting antibiotic polymyxin B. During infection, T3SS effector OspC1 prevents septin recruitment, while stress-response regulator cspC protects against septin-mediated changes to membrane potential. Hence, septin binding is intrinsically antibacterial and is sensed by Shigella as a danger signal to promote mechanisms of intracellular tolerance.

items.title: Mechanically driven grain refinement in Mo by nanoindentation pop-ins: A case of transient instability
items.summary_raw: During load-controlled nanoindentation of pristine metals, the homogeneous dislocation nucleation manifests as a sudden displacement burst, or pop-in, associated with shear stresses approaching the theoretical strength, massive dislocation nucleation, and rapid yet uncontrolled indenter penetration. Here, we show that manually terminating nanoindentation immediately after the first pop-in enables direct access to a transient deformation and reveals unexpected microstructural transformations in molybdenum (Mo). Using single-crystal Mo with different surface orientations, we demonstrate pop-in-induced nucleation of new, highly misoriented grains at room temperature. This nucleation behavior is attributed to two mechanically driven processes: 1) activation of twinning followed by the evolution of twin boundaries into random high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) and 2) rearrangement of dislocations into HAGBs within regions of high local dislocation density during the abrupt deformation accompanying the pop-in. Displacement-controlled atomistic simulations reproduce both twin- and dislocation-mediated grain nucleation within an individual grain when a preexisting grain boundary blocks dislocation glide. However, in the absence of such a grain boundary, nucleated dislocations glide into the surrounding crystal and fail to form new grains. Continued indentation beyond pop-in mechanically erases newly formed grains, as confirmed in both experiments and simulations, explaining why…

items.title: Holocene millennial climate variability influenced by tropical–Antarctic ocean–atmosphere interactions
items.summary_raw: A prominent unstable feature, millennial-scale climate oscillation (MCO), punctuated the Holocene. Solar activity and deep ocean variability are generally regarded as the origin of the MCO, yet the dynamics remain debated. Using a Holocene transient simulation with the EC-Earth climate model (8 to 0 ka BP), together with a global compilation of 304 temperature reconstructions, here we identify a robust ~1,350-y oscillatory mode that characterizes Holocene climate variability and is self-sustained and crucially influenced by tropical–Antarctic ocean–atmosphere interactions. Within each cycle, Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) strengthening evolves with the developing warming and an El Niño-like tropical sea surface temperature (SST) response, accompanied by anticyclonic circulation anomalies over the high-latitude Southern Ocean. Northward cold advection of the associated enhanced westerly winds off the Antarctic coast overcomes the effect of sea ice retreat to promote AABW formation, ocean stratification, and warming. Positive feedbacks including sea ice-albedo, tropical air–sea interaction, and SST-AABW magnify surface warming till AABW reaches its peak. Thereafter, reduced brine rejection from sea-ice retreat weakens AABW, counteracts the warming, and commences a switch to its cooling phase. The dominant periodicity, consistent with that inferred from proxy reconstructions, is confirmed by complementary climate simulations. These results provide an alternative physical…

items.title: Revised estimates of types and duration of long COVID symptoms based on claims records from 245 million US patients
items.summary_raw: COVID-19 has been reported to cause multisystem effects lasting years [Z. Al-Aly, E. Topol, Science 383, 830–832 (2024)]. These findings are primarily based on cohort studies comparing test-positive COVID-19 patients to controls without known COVID-19 infection, tested or untested [M. Cai, Y. Xie, E. J. Topol, Z. Al-Aly, Nat. Med. 30, 1564–1573 (2024)]. However, such comparisons can be biased by the reasons people were tested. Using 14.4 billion insurance claims from 244.7 million US patients, we find that most long-term effects attributed to COVID-19 by unrestricted control designs likely reflect bias due to selective testing of individuals with non-COVID conditions, causing long-term effects of those conditions to be misattributed to COVID-19. We removed this bias by analyzing only tested individuals, comparing test-positive to test-negative patients. Across 614 clinical outcomes followed over 2 y, the test-based design resulted in 83.5% fewer symptoms being attributable to COVID-19 between 30 to 119 d after infection (43 attributable symptoms vs. 262 for the unrestricted control design), a 98.2% reduction at 120 to 359 d (5 vs. 286), and a 100% reduction at 360 to 719 d (0 vs. 369). The unrestricted control design also attributed unrelated outcomes (e.g., firearm injuries) to COVID-19 at a high rate, whereas the testing-based design did not. The test-based control design may modestly underestimate some effects. This study does not indicate that symptoms beyond one year…

items.title: An innervated and vascularized HNSCC-on-a-chip model built on defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices
items.summary_raw: Understanding the tumor microenvironment requires experimental platforms that faithfully recapitulate its key components. Here, we present an innervated and vascularized head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)-on-a-chip platform built with fully defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices (eECMs). In a stepwise increase of complexity, we first cocultured patient-derived HNSCC cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and endothelial cells within tailored eECMs, revealing extracellular matrix-dependent differences in transcriptional state, multicellular self-organization, and chemotherapeutic sensitivity. We then integrated these three-dimensional constructs into a cancer–vasculature interface, which enabled analysis of eECM-dependent directional collective migration and invasion. Finally, we incorporated trigeminal innervation through injectable 3D human bioengineered trigeminal ganglia, establishing a chip-based innervation–tumor–vasculature tri-interface. Together, this all-human platform integrates fully defined ECM, vasculature, and innervation in a single modular system to investigate tumor organization, invasion, and therapeutic responses within a controlled human microenvironment.

items.title: Imaging real-space chiral rotation of flat-band states in helical trilayer graphene
items.summary_raw: Flat bands have been experimentally realized in a wide variety of graphene-based moiré systems with designed stacking configurations. While these moiré systems feature similar flat-band structures, they differ markedly in key characteristics, such as band flattening, band isolation, and band topology, which give rise to their distinct strongly correlated phases. Here, we present a systematic real-space investigation comparing flat-band states across four representative graphene moiré systems, revealing a characteristic chiral rotation of flat-band states within helical trilayer graphene. Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we directly observe that ultra-small twist-angle helical trilayer graphene unveils distinct threefold-anisotropic electronic states localized at certain moiré sites within the flat-band regime, distinguishing it from the other moiré systems investigated in this study. Spatial mapping of the threefold-anisotropic pattern reveals a chiral rotation that varies as a function of energy. Theoretical simulations based on the Bistritzer–MacDonald model reproduce the distinct orientations of the threefold-anisotropic patterns across different low-energy minibands and reveal a systematic correspondence between the direction of local density-of-states rotation and the structural chirality of helical trilayer graphene. Our results demonstrate that real-space electronic textures—previously overlooked—can partially reveal the intrinsic disparities…

items.title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression
items.summary_raw: Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log 10 at 3 mo postpartum, “controllers”) and 12 with more stable levels (“noncontrollers”). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody…

items.title: Revisiting atmospheric sulfur chemistry: Acid-catalyzed pathways do not control H 2 SO 4 formation
items.summary_raw: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO 4 ) drives new particle formation and radiatively important aerosol processes in the atmosphere, but its formation pathways remain poorly resolved because of limited kinetics data. To clarify these pathways, we combined coupled-cluster calculations, reaction rate theory, and a global chemistry transport model to quantify acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration and its atmospheric significance. We find that the overall kinetics is not governed by a tight transition state but rather is controlled by a preceding loose transition state associated with the formation of the precursor complex of the acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration. Our results reverse a recent view that acid catalysis is the dominant contributor to atmospheric SO 3 hydration, instead supporting an earlier view that water catalysis dominates SO 3 hydration. Incorporating the revised kinetics into the GEOS-Chem atmospheric model reveals no significant impact of acid-catalyzed SO 3 hydration on the simulated concentrations of H 2 SO 4 . The present findings highlight the critical roles of variational transition states in kinetic modeling.

items.title: Intraventricular clindamycin enhances interstitial brain fluid drainage and the blood–brain barrier after a traumatic brain injury
items.summary_raw: Despite advances in the acute clinical management of severe traumatic brain injuries (TBIs), treating injury-derived secondary pathogenesis remains challenging. We demonstrate intracerebroventricular (I.C.V.) administration of clindamycin alleviates TBI secondary pathogenesis in both focal and diffuse murine models of brain injury. I.C.V. administration of clindamycin increased the motility of ependymal cilia, which line the ventricles and spinal canal, by 30 to 60%, which correlated with interstitial brain fluid drainage through the cortex (r > 0.9 Pearson, n = 4 compounds tested). I.C.V. clindamycin treatment post-TBI also restored the blood–brain barrier (BBB), decreased lesion size, and lowered serum levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein by 2.8-fold. Consistent with these data, a novel objective recognition test revealed an improvement in recognition memory in brain-injured mice treated with clindamycin. These collective findings reveal a counterintuitive finding that I.C.V. clindamycin enhances drainage of toxins from the brain while simultaneously restoring the BBB, potentially providing a new solution for alleviating secondary pathogenesis in brain-injured patients.

items.title: Regulation of miR-219 and its target RalGPS is essential for synaptic plasticity at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction
items.summary_raw: RNA regulatory mechanisms mediate adaptive responses relying on rapid changes in gene expression. By examining microRNA (miRNA)-mediated control of structural synaptic plasticity, we find miR-219 and five other conserved miRNAs regulate activity-induced morphogenesis at Drosophila glutamatergic synapses. Among miRNA targets downregulated by acute stimulation, the Ral activating factor RalGPS is necessary for presynaptic morphogenesis and is sufficient to block plasticity. We find that RalGPS must be held within a narrow range of expression for structural remodeling to occur. Loss or excess of RalGPS both abolish activity-induced synapse growth. Without altering levels of mature miR-219, stimulation elevates miR-219 loading in Argonaute (Ago1)-containing complexes that mediate miRNA gene silencing. We also find that elevated Protein Kinase A activity suppresses miR-219 association with Ago1 and blocks activity-induced synaptic growth, suggesting that miRNA loading and unloading in neurons are both controlled by activity-dependent regulation of Ago1.

items.title: Neuromodulation-inspired gated associative memory networks: Extended memory retrieval and emergent multistability
items.summary_raw: Classical autoassociative memory models have been central to understanding emergent computations in recurrent neural circuits across diverse biological contexts. However, they typically neglect neuromodulatory agents that are known to strongly shape memory capacity and stability. Here we introduce a minimal, biophysically motivated associative memory network in which neuromodulator-like signals are modeled by a self-adaptive, activity-dependent gating mechanism. Using many-body simulations and dynamical mean-field theory, we show that such gating fundamentally reorganizes the attractor structure: the network bypasses the classical spin-glass transition, maintaining robust, high-overlap retrieval far beyond the standard critical capacity. Mechanistically, when the gates act as fully open or fully closed switches, the gate stabilizes transient “ghost” remnants of stored patterns even far above the Hopfield limit, converting a single memory fixed-point attractor into a cluster of fixed points. The retrieved state is set by the initial overlap rather than quantized to the stored pattern. This graded dependence may be exploited for input-driven computation with persistent activity. These results establish that neuromodulation-like gating alone—without modifying synaptic weights or introducing explicit higher-order couplings—can dramatically expand memory capacity, eliminate catastrophic breakdown, and reshape a discrete attractor landscape into a rich continuum, suggesting a…

items.title: SMYD3-catalyzed dimethylation of gasdermin D at lysine 43 promotes pyroptosis and inflammatory responses
items.summary_raw: Gasdermin D (GSDMD), a key pyroptosis effector downstream of inflammasome activation, undergoes precise regulation by multiple posttranslational modifications. Here, we identify SMYD3, a lysine methyltransferase, as a positive regulator of GSDMD. SMYD3 interacts with GSDMD and catalyzes its dimethylation at lysine 43. This modification promotes GSDMD cleavage by caspases, leading to increased oligomerization and membrane localization of GSDMD N-terminal fragment (GSDMD-NT), which ultimately induces pyroptosis. Disrupting or inhibiting SMYD3 alleviates overactivated inflammation, thereby protecting against lipopolysaccharide-induced death in mice and zebrafish. Our findings reveal a role for SMYD3 in regulating the inflammatory response and shed light on a new mechanism that modulates GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis.

items.title: Stress-inducible WASF3 regulates brain metabolism and cognitive function
items.summary_raw: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome protein family member 3 (WASF3) disrupts mitochondrial respiration and is induced in association with endoplasmic reticulum stress in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Because cognitive impairment is a hallmark of ME/CFS, we investigated the role of WASF3 in brain metabolism and function using WASF3 transgenic and knockout mouse models. WASF3 disrupted respiratory complex IV and localized to mitochondria-associated membranes, known to modulate cellular processes important for neuronal activity. Overexpression of WASF3 in the hippocampus, a critical region for memory formation, induced a metabolic shift toward glycolysis and promoted a “hypometabolic” state. Increased WASF3 also caused a reduction in ATPIF1, previously shown to facilitate cognitive function, and impaired learning. Conversely, WASF3 deficiency increased ATPIF1 level, enhanced oxidative metabolism, and preserved cognitive function under stress. Together, these findings demonstrate that WASF3 suppresses oxidative metabolism in the brain and contributes to cognitive dysfunction, providing mechanistic insights into the “brain fog” reported in ME/CFS.

items.title: A voltage-gated porin PPE1 regulates secretion and drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
items.summary_raw: Drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ) remains a formidable clinical hurdle, compounded by the fact that the pathways by which antibiotics penetrate its multilayered cell envelope remain incompletely mapped. We identify PPE1 as a voltage-gated outer-membrane porin that mediates the secretion of kupyaphores while also facilitating the uptake of the frontline anti-tubercular drug isoniazid (INH). Genome-wide association analysis of 38,038 clinical isolates links ppe1 mutations with INH resistance, highlighting its clinical relevance. Consistent with this, the Mtb Δ ppe1 mutant shows increased tolerance to INH, accompanied by markedly reduced intracellular accumulation of INH compared with the wild-type strain. The Δ ppe1 strain exhibits attenuated infection, impaired growth, and reduced virulence in a murine infection model. Electron microscopy, molecular modeling, and single-channel electrophysiology reveal that PPE1 assembles into an unusual pentameric α-helical channel, distinct from classical β-barrel bacterial porins. Together, our findings identify PPE1 as a key determinant of mycobacterial membrane permeability that coordinates metallophore secretion and also antibiotic influx. This work uncovers a previously unrecognized mechanism governing Mtb physiology, virulence, and drug susceptibility, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: Viral metagenomics reveals heterogeneity in mammalian virus hosting, sharing, and spillover
items.summary_raw: Zoonotic viruses originating from mammals pose a persistent threat to global health. While rodents and bats are often considered “special reservoirs,” it is debated if spillover risk is driven by specific taxa or merely reflects mammalian species richness. However, most tests have focused on published host–virus association datasets, which can reflect systematic biases in host and virus sampling effort. To address this limitation, we analyzed a comprehensive repository of 4,685 metagenomic datasets, minimizing bias toward any one viral taxon and spanning 296 species across 14 mammalian orders. We characterized the global mammalian virome and found substantial heterogeneity in the capacity of different mammalian orders to harbor and share human-associated viruses. Counter to conventional wisdom, carnivores exhibited significantly higher propensities to carry human-associated viruses, with bats ranked lower in this metric of zoonotic risk. Network analyses of viral sharing further revealed higher cross-order virus sharing among specific mammalian orders (e.g., carnivores and artiodactyls). Phylogenetic comparative analyses revealed that host life-history traits (e.g., longevity) and anthropogenic factors (e.g., urban land use) were key ecological drivers of both virus richness and transmission centrality. Our study provides a data-driven framework that challenges prevailing narratives of zoonotic risk and offers a refined strategy for prioritizing surveillance and mitigating…

items.title: Protein resource allocation across subcellular compartments revealed by large-scale absolute quantitative proteomics in yeast
items.summary_raw: Subcellular compartmentalization within complex membrane-bound organelles is a hallmark of eukaryal life, enabling metabolic specialization through spatial segregation. Here, we compiled a dataset encompassing 300 absolute quantitative proteomes, the largest to date, across two yeast species under diverse experimental conditions. Leveraging big data analysis, formula fitting, and machine learning, quantitative correlations among protein abundance, resource allocation, and cellular phenotypes were elucidated at a system level. We found that subcellular resource distribution is highly uneven and covaries with specific growth rate. Specifically, at high specific growth rates, the protein mass fraction (PMF) from certain compartments, (e.g., nucleus) is consistently reduced, coinciding with the increasing protein resource demand from ribosomes. Meanwhile, nutrient limitation may induce resource recycling by upregulating protein resources within specific compartments (e.g., vacuole) to sustain stress adaptation. Importantly, our integrative analysis indicates that PMF from a few subcellular compartments (e.g., nucleus and ribosomes) can accurately predict yeast physiological parameters (e.g., specific growth rate, oxygen uptake rate), and a limited protein set (≥ 23) could be used to capture the variation in resource allocation across seven major subcellular compartments. Furthermore, our comparative analysis between Crabtree-positive and Crabtree-negative species across…

items.title: Encoding metal coordination pathways and nuclearity by molecular knotting
items.summary_raw: Precise control over the nuclearity and spatial organization of metal ions is a central objective in coordination chemistry. Knotting imposes severe geometric constraints on frameworks but has rarely been exploited to organize inequivalent metal-binding sites within a single ligand. Here we report that a molecular cinquefoil knot containing both bidentate and tridentate chelating sites enables programmed metal-ion coordination pathways. Direct metalation affords Mn(II) 5 -, Fe(II) 5 -, Co(II) 5 -, and Cd(II) 5 -knots through a dinuclear intermediate and an unusual 2-to-5 metal nuclearity progression, even though these metals do not template knot formation. Crystallization of a Mn(II) 2 -intermediate reveals partial demetalation but retains a Mn(II) center displaying a “3 + 3” coordination mode, whereas all Fe(II) ions in the fully metalated Fe(II) 5 -knot adopt a “3 + 2” binding geometry. Together with computational simulations, these observations support a stepwise metalation mechanism in which the dinuclear “3 + 3” coordination environment evolves into the “3 + 2” motif of the pentanuclear knot. Although the Ni(II) 5 - knot cannot be obtained by direct metalation because of slow incorporation, it forms readily via transmetalation from a Zn(II) 5 -knot. Circular dichroism measurements show that chiral expression is dictated by the overall ligand arrangement rather than the identity of the metal ions. The work demonstrates molecular knotting as a strategy for…

items.title: Annexins cooperate with Myomaker to promote myoblast fusion
items.summary_raw: Myoblast fusion is essential for skeletal muscle development and regeneration. Myomaker is a muscle-specific fusogen indispensable for this process. Cryoelectron microscopy analysis has shown that Myomaker dimerization is required for myoblast fusion and muscle formation. However, the precise molecular mechanisms of Myomaker function remain unclear. Notably, the short extracellular domain of Myomaker suggests the involvement of additional proteins that cooperate with Myomaker to facilitate membrane fusion. To identify potential interacting partners of Myomaker, we employed an APEX2-based proximity labeling approach in a synchronized myoblast fusion and differentiation system. By comparing results with a fusion-deficient mutant form of Myomaker, we identified several members of the Annexin family of calcium-dependent phospholipid-binding proteins as prominent candidates for interaction, particularly under prefusion conditions. Among these, Annexins A2, A5, and A6 were found to colocalize with Myomaker at the myoblast plasma membrane. Proximity ligation assays further confirmed the close association of these Annexins with Myomaker at the cell surface. Functional analyses demonstrated that these Annexins can promote heterologous cell–cell fusion between fibroblasts and myoblasts. While single knockdown of Annexin A2, A5, or A6 had minimal effects, the simultaneous knockdown of all three impaired myoblast fusion, indicating functional redundancy among them. Together, these…

High power bills, blackouts land Michigan utilities on the ballot
items.summary_raw: When 83-year-old Sam Getsinger thinks about the future, she pictures her five grandchildren and the world she wants to leave them. An important part of that world, Getsinger said, is a healthy democracy. So when she first heard about an initiative to limit Michigan utilities’ influence in political campaigns, she immediately volunteered to support it. “I don’t want our politics to continue so that the person with the most money wins everything,” Getsinger said. “I don’t think that’s a very sound democracy.” Getsinger spent months knocking on doors throughout northern Michigan. She said nearly all the people behind those doors agreed with her that utilities shouldn’t wield as much political influence as they do. Keeping corporate money out of elections is notoriously difficult in the United States, but next week Michiganders are going to vote on whether they should try it anyway, with a particular focus on the state’s electricity and gas utilities. Saying they are sick of power outages and high bills, advocacy groups and volunteers are pushing for a ballot measure they say will roll back utilities’ influence over state elections, freeing lawmakers to hold them accountable. Polls from supportive organizations show strong voter approval of the initiative, but even if it passes, and even if it survives legal challenges, some experts say it still won’t get all utility money out of politics. As extreme heat worsens, renters are gaining a ‘right to cooling’
items.summary_raw: Subjecting the incarcerated residents of Texas to extreme heat constitutes cruel and unusual punishment, and prisons statewide must install air-conditioning by the end of 2029. Although the ruling Judge Robert Pitman issued last month is unique in its invocation of the Constitution’s Eighth Amendment, it is an explicit recognition of an idea increasingly reflected in laws and policies nationwide: As extreme heat becomes more dangerous , even deadly , access to cooling is increasingly seen as a necessity rather than a luxury. This shift has been especially active in housing, where renters often face structural hurdles to accessing cool air, from high costs to explicit bans on the installation of air-conditioning. This summer, jurisdictions across the U.S. passed policies setting maximum indoor temperatures, requiring landlords to provide AC, or otherwise expanding tenants’ access to cooling. The state of Maryland, for instance, said property owners with 10 or more units must install AC if they renovate. In Spokane, Washington, where 14 people died during a heat wave in July, landlords must now provide “ adequate cooling ” in at least one room of each unit. “You can no longer responsibly rent a place if you don’t have a way of keeping it cool, because people will die,” said Brian Henning, director of the Institute for Climate, Water, and the Environment at Gonzaga University and a leading advocate for the Spokane policy. Regime-dependent performance of green and brown energy Exchange-Traded Funds under climate policy uncertainty: the role of investor sentiment
items.summary_raw: This study examines whether the returns of green and brown energy Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) are exposed to climate policy uncertainty (CPU), whether this exposure differs between low- and high-volatility market regimes, and whether investor sentiment moderates it. Using monthly data for five green and five brown US-listed energy ETFs from May 2015 to April 2026, a two-state Markov regime-switching model is estimated, with the AAII bull-bear spread employed as a measure of investor sentiment. The estimated regimes are persistent volatility states; for brown ETFs, the high-volatility regime spans the COVID-19 crash, the subsequent recovery and the 2022 energy-price shock. The most important finding is a divergence between the two groups, specifically, increases in CPU are associated with higher returns for all five brown ETFs in the low-volatility regime and for two funds in the high-volatility regime, whereas green ETF returns show no systematic relationship with the CPU index. This divergence is confirmed by a single-regime benchmark and by a green-minus-brown portfolio that accounts for the high correlation among brown funds, and it is robust to controls for extreme market episodes. However, when the November 2016 and November 2024 election months are controlled for, the low-volatility CPU coefficient remains significant at the 5% level only for IXC, so part of the brown exposure comes from these 2 months. items.title: Government positions and climate change: paradigmatic conflict versus consensus in environmental performance
items.summary_raw: Historically, environmental policy was framed as a fundamental trade-off between economic growth and ecological preservation. Since the mid-1980s, however, this dichotomy has been largely replaced by the paradigm of ecological modernization, expressed in concepts like “green growth” and “sustainable development,” which hold that economic growth and environmental protection are mutually reinforcing. This shift was accompanied by the assumption that a broad political consensus on reconciling economic growth and environmental protection would lead to superior environmental outcomes. Yet, the persistent gap between climate targets and actual emission trends necessitates a critical re-evaluation of this “consensus” approach and of whether the original antagonism between environmental protection and economic growth has genuinely been overcome. To assess this claim, this study tests six distinct conceptualizations of government ideology and policy focus, analyzing government positions across 35 advanced democracies from 1990 to 2021. The findings show that neither the focus on technocratic environmental issues, nor the classic left-right divide, nor the newer, more encompassing green-alternative versus traditional-authoritarian dimension predicts emissions performance. Instead, emissions decline where governments adopt growth-critical positions and even more where environmental ideology contrasts growth-oriented productionism with growth-critical environmental protection. items.title: Warming world, informed care: Piloting a script to guide climate conversations in healthcare
items.source_name: The Journal of Climate Change and Health
items.summary_raw: Introduction While including climate change in patient health counseling offers several potential benefits, research on provider-patient communication about the climate-health connection is limited. To better understand how physicians can introduce climate-health education into patient encounters, researchers (two medical doctors in a climate-and-health equity fellowship and a climate communication scientist) developed and piloted a brief provider-patient counseling script. Results Patient reactions were largely positive. Challenges faced by clinicians included lack of time to implement additional patient education during routine visits and concerns about lack of economic reimbursement. Conclusion Although a nascent step, this study may help other physicians begin these crucial conversations with their patients.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Factors Influencing High-Quality Energy Development at the Provincial Level in China
items.summary_raw: Promoting high-quality energy development is of great significance for achieving China's “dual carbon” goals and ensuring high-quality economic development. Therefore, this paper places high-quality energy development within the context of high-quality economic development. This article also reveals, from a systems perspective, the four-dimensional synergy mechanism of “innovation and openness, economic efficiency, low-carbon and clean-development, and safety and reliability”. The entropy method is used to measure the development level of China's energy system and subsystems. The Moran index (Moran's I) and kernel density estimation are combined to analyze the systems' clustering characteristics, regional differences, and spatial evolution patterns. Co-linearity tests and two-way fixed-effects models are used to identify the factors that influence high-quality development. The results show the following: (1) China's high-quality coordinated energy development continues to improve, but regional development and growth remain uneven. The development level is highest in the east, followed by central and western regions, and is lowest in the northeast. (2) The economic efficiency and green and low-carbon subsystems have developed well. items.title: Reimagining nature finance
items.summary_raw: Natural capital markets (NCMs) are widely heralded as an important solution to the biodiversity crisis. Extensive effort, energy, time, and resources have been invested into making them function. NCMs are intended to catalyse financial flows from the private sector to conservation and nature recovery projects, helping to close the ‘nature finance gap’. Whilst this rhetoric is appealing, there is growing evidence that NCMs (principally voluntary biodiversity and carbon offset markets) are unlikely to ever protect or recover nature at the necessary scale and speed required, nor deliver wide-ranging socio-ecological benefits to a diversity of communities, organisms, and ecosystems. Drawing on interdisciplinary evidence, we outline five established flaws associated with NCMs: persistent barriers to scaling, a compensatory rather than restorative character, the prioritisation of financial returns over socio-ecological outcomes, justice and equity concerns, and measurement challenges. Collectively, they lead us to offer a central claim: NCMs have absorbed a disproportionate amount of political and research attention relative to their limited impact. We call for reimagining nature finance, based on a central tenet: raising funds should be a means to an end, not an end in itself.
